The present preregistered systematic review and meta-analysis (https://osf.io/u4e25/?view_only=723a3f72fdf648d5a5be1deea72b8e7e) explores the roots of the relationship between EF and intelligence and their sub-components in development, including only individuals under 18 years of age. A systematic search was conducted in the databases PsycInfo and PubMed on September 21st 2022 and supplemented by a search for grey literature. K = 2149 studies were extracted and coded. Included are studies that examine a healthy sample under 18 years of age, measure the primary variables “intelligence” and “executive functions” as separate constructs and assess them with standardized behavioral instruments. For EF, separate meta-analyses with a conglomerate EF-measure and the sub-components memory updating, inhibition and set shifting are conducted. For intelligence, separate meta-analyses are conducted employing the “g”-factor and fluid intelligence. In a preliminary analysis, the data from k = 9 studies with n = 4,178 minors (3-17 years) were included in the model, resulting in a mean effect size of r = 0.45 [0.37,0.53] for the association between EF and the “g”-factor. There was little evidence for publication bias (funnel plot, trim-and-fill method: n = 0, Rosenthal’s Fail-Safe N =2658). Consistent with this pattern, EF were also positively associated with fluid intelligence. The random-effects meta-analysis (k = 15; n = 7,362) yielded a moderate to strong correlation (r = .54, 95% CI [.41, .64]). This study empirically clarifies the overlap between two broad cognitive constructs spanning separate research traditions to further our understanding of children’s cognitive structure.

242. Orthographic Processing in Bilinguals German-French Readers
Claire Gigleux | Université du Luxembourg | Luxembourg
Show details
Authors:
Claire Gigleux | Université du Luxembourg | Luxembourg
Dr. Aliette Lochy | Luxembourg

According to grain-size theory, transparent languages such as German promote fine-grained sublexical processing based on reliable grapheme–phoneme correspondences, whereas opaque languages like French require larger orthographic units and stronger reliance on the lexical route.
Twenty-six Luxembourgish children (9.70 ± 0.64 years old; L1 German, L2 French) completed a letter-choice task to measure the Word Superiority Effect (WSE), which differentiates sublexical from lexical processing across languages at the behavioral level. The influence of orthographic opacity on the neural reading network was assessed using Fast Periodic Visual Stimulation with EEG. Participants viewed rapid sequences of stimuli (6 Hz) for 60 seconds in either French or German, with a real word inserted every fifth stimulus (1.2 Hz). Discrimination of words from the pseudoword base elicited neural responses at 1.2 Hz and its harmonics. Words varied by condition and consisted of: (i) simple GPCs (1 letter = 1 sound), (ii) complex GPCs (2+ letters = 1 sound), or (iii) irregular words (French only), while the pseudowords always consisted of simple GPCs.
The WSE and word-selective neural responses are expected to be stronger in French, where orthographic opacity favors whole-word recognition. This study will clarify orthographic depth modulates the emergence and characteristics of lexical representations in bilinguals

243. Evaluating an Alternative Approach to Fitting Regression Trees in (Multilevel) Meta-Analyses
Richard Woermann | Münster University | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Richard Woermann | Münster University | Germany
Dr. Katrin Jansen
Prof. Dr. Steffen Nestler

A central goal of meta-analysis is to explain heterogeneity in effect sizes through moderator analysis. Meta-regression, which is the standard approach to this problem, lacks automated variable selection and requires a priori specification of non-linear patterns and interactions. Meta-regression trees seem to be a promising alternative that are free of these limitations and yield results that are easily interpretable. An algorithm for fitting meta-regression trees is implemented in the R package metacart. This algorithm assumes the effect sizes to be independent, yet researchers in psychology often want to account for multilevel structures in their meta-analyses. An alternative approach that can also be applied to multilevel-structures is to adapt mixed-effects regression trees to meta-analysis. We aim to evaluate the performance achieved with this approach in comparison to metacart by conducting a simulation study. We will assess how both algorithms perform in terms of variable selection and prediction in two- and three-level meta-analysis. Our results aim to inform about the feasibility, strengths and limitations of using regression trees for moderator analysis in (multilevel) meta-analysis.

244. Motor decision-making in social interaction: Investigating joint action coordination in the object-transfer task
Prof. Dr. Matthias Weigelt | Paderborn University, Germany | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Prof. Dr. Matthias Weigelt | Paderborn University, Germany | Germany
Jean-Luca Schulz | Paderborn University, Germany
Toni Anton Schirmacher | Paderborn University, Germany
Prof. Dr. Natalie Sebanz | Central European University (CEU) in Vienna, Austria

Török et al. (2019, Psychological Science) showed that people minimize collective costs in virtual joint-action tasks. Here, we examine coordination efficiency in a real-world setting with two partners navigating through environmental constraints under varying physical loads. Forty participants (18 females; M = 22.5 years) transported a ball from one corner to the diagonally opposite corner of a 10 × 10 m square. A horizontal barrier with two gaps and a vertical barrier of equal or unequal length created five different path asymmetries. Partner A started and chose a gap to pass the ball to Partner B, determining the initial subpath. In congruent trials, shorter initial paths led to shorter total paths; in incongruent trials, the shorter initial path resulted in a longer total path; in neutral trials, both paths were equal. Partners completed the dyads under three physical load conditions: either none, one, or both partners wore a weighted vest. Results showed a strong preference for initial subpaths minimizing aggregate path length, especially when path asymmetry was high. Importantly, physical load influenced motor-decision making in a way that participants adjusted their initial path choices to reduce the effort for the more burdened partner. These findings reveal flexible, cost-sensitive motor planning that integrates environmental structure, individual effort, and shared task demands. Coordination efficiency emerges through embodied, interactive processes that dynamically optimize collective outcomes. This study demonstrates that real-world joint actions are guided by adaptive, socially sensitive strategies aimed at minimizing shared costs, highlighting the role of embodied cognition in cooperative behavior.

245. Selbstselektion von Studienteilnehmenden durch informed consent in der Thanatopsychologie?
Holger Busch | Universität Trier | Germany
Show details
Author:
Holger Busch | Universität Trier | Germany

In der thanatopsychologischen Forschung stehen möglicherweise zwei Kriterien guter Forschung miteinander in Konflikt: Einerseits sollen sich interessierte Personen aufgrund umfassender Informationen für eine Teilnahme entscheiden können. Andererseits kann die Vorabinformation, dass die Studie den Tod thematisiert, zu einem Selbstselektionsbias führen, weil Menschen mit ausgeprägter Angst vor dem Tod erst gar nicht teilnehmen. Die vorliegende Studie untersucht, wie groß diese Problematik tatsächlich ist. Dazu wurden Versuchspersonen randomisiert einer von drei Bedingungen zugeteilt: „naive“, „informierte“ oder „Trigger Warnung“ Teilnahme (ohne Vorabnennung des Themas Tod; mit Vorabnennung; mit Vorabnennung inkl. Verweis, dass Personen, denen das Thema zu nahe gehen könnte, lieber auf die Teilnahme verzichten sollten). Anschließend sollten die Versuchspersonen die Studienteilnahme bestätigen und ggf. einen Selbstauskunftsfragebogen zur Angst vor dem Tod ausfüllen. Insgesamt begannen 543 Personen im Alter von 18 bis 88 Jahren (M = 39.44; SD = 15.56) die Fragebogenbearbeitung (78% weiblich, 21% männlich). Tatsächlich war die Abbruchquote noch vor dem Selbstauskunftsfragebogen zur Angst vor dem Tod in der Bedingung „Trigger Warnung“ höher (9%) als in den beiden anderen („naiv“: 3%; „informiert“: 4%), χ2(2) = 6.29, p = .043. Es gab keinen signifikanten Unterschied zwischen den Gruppen bzgl. eines späteren Abbruchs der Fragebogenbearbeitung, χ2(2) = 3.88, p = .144. Ebenso ergab sich kein signifikanter Mittelwertsunterschied zwischen den Bedingungen bezüglich Angst vor dem Tod, F(2, 442) = 2.30, p = .102. Die Ergebnisse legen nahe, dass unterschiedliche Vorabinformationen zu unterschiedlichen Abbruchquoten führen können, dieser Unterschied aber nicht gleichbedeutend mit systematischen Mittelwertsunterschieden in der Angst vor dem Tod ist.

246. Proactive Work Behavior and Employee Wellbeing: A Meta-Analytic Investigation
Nele Normann | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Nele Normann | Germany
Dr. Clara Kühner
Dr. Maie Stein
Prof. Dr. Hannes Zacher

Modern workplaces are characterized by work intensification and heightened flexibility, which lead to growing expectations for employees to actively shape their work environment. Consequently, proactive work behavior (PWB) – self-initiated, future-oriented actions to improve oneself and one’s work environment – has gained significant research attention. However, its implications for employee wellbeing (EWB) are so far not well understood. Research indicates PWB may be “energizing”, fostering autonomy and competence and thereby enhancing positive wellbeing indicators such as vitality and engagement. On the other hand, PWB may be “depleting,” requiring sustained effort and self- regulation that can increase stress and exhaustion. Given this dual nature of PWB, it is essential to understand the associations between PWB and EWB. This study provides the first systematic meta-analysis of the PWB–EWB relationship, extending previous narrative reviews. We present a preregistered meta-analysis that quantitatively synthesizes associations between different types of PWB (e.g., personal initiative, taking charge, voice) and both positive and negative EWB indicators. Following PRISMA-oriented procedures, we searched major databases (June–August 2025), screened conference proceedings and reached out to authors to capture unpublished work (October–November 2025). The current dataset comprises 224 independent studies with 231 samples and a total sample size of more than 115,000 employees. The evidence base is dominated by cross-sectional designs, and most studies were published in recent years (2020-2024). Across measures, job crafting and work engagement are assessed most frequently. By the time of the colloquium, the meta-analysis will be completed, and key results will be presented.

247. Anomaly Detection in Psychology: A Systematic Review
Loreen Sabel | TU Dortmund University | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Loreen Sabel | TU Dortmund University | Germany
Prof. Dr. Philipp Doebler | TU Dortmund University | Germany

Anomalies are rare instances in a dataset that behave differently from the majority of the observations. In contrast to mere outlier removal, one focuses on observations that deviate from the common pattern and assumes them to be informative. For example, deviations from normal behavior can be indicative of relapses in a clinical context. Another example are aberrant test takers, such as careless responders. Methods to detect anomalies range from classical statistical methods like Mahalanobis distance to shallow machine learning methods like isolation forest and deep neural networks such as autoencoders. The latter two classes of methods are typically researched from an algorithmic viewpoint with industrial domains in mind. A prominent example is fraud detection in financial transactions. Currently, machine learning methods for anomaly detection are applied sporadically and unsystematically in psychological research. We present results from our pre-registered systematic review of multivariate anomaly detection methods in the psychological literature. Based on a broad exploratory search term, we screened 6406 abstracts and 193 full texts. We find applications of a large variety of anomaly detection methods across many psychological subfields. A typical paper reports an exploratory use of a single anomaly detection method. We characterize the identified methods and provide an overview of their application aims. Given the industrial background of many anomaly detection methods, we discuss challenges for their application to human behavior data.

248. Exploring the Causal Robustness of Cross-Lagged Effects in Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Models
Alexander Starlinger | Helmut Schmidt Universität Hamburg | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Alexander Starlinger | Helmut Schmidt Universität Hamburg | Germany
Prof. Dr. Steffen Zitzmann | MSH Medical School Hamburg - University of Applied Sciences and Medical University
Prof. Drew Halford Bailey | University of California, Irvine | United States
Prof. Dr. Kou Murayama | Hector Research Institute of Education Sciences and Psychology, University of Tübingen
Prof. Dr. Nicolas Hübner | Universität Bonn
Prof. Dr. Martin Hecht | Helmut Schmidt Universität Hamburg | Germany

The random intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM) is widely used in psychology to study reciprocal longitudinal effects while accounting for unobserved time-stable, trait-like confounding. Recent work suggests that the robustness of the RI-CLPM against omitted variables extends beyond time-stable confounders. The random intercept component can “absorb” and thus reduce causal bias due to omitted time-varying covariate processes, though at the expense of creating illusory trait variance (Bailey et al., 2024). However, evidence for this compensation effect has largely been limited to cases in which omitted covariate processes primarily affect a single focal process. In contrast, related work indicates that when omitted covariate processes act as longitudinal mediators or common causes, the RI-CLPM can yield biased or even spurious cross-lagged effects.

We examined how broadly the causal robustness of the RI-CLPM generalizes, using analytical bias formulas for lagged effects under omitted covariate processes (Robitzsch & Lüdtke, 2025). We conducted a systematic numerical study in which key parameters were varied to represent three causal roles of omitted variables: (a) influences affecting only one process, (b) variables that confound both processes, and (c) variables that act as longitudinal mediators between processes. Robustness is evaluated using the compensation rate, which quantifies the extent to which bias in lagged effects in the traditional CLPM is reduced by the RI-CLPM.

The study offers a systematic characterization of bias compensation in the RI-CLPM, clarifying the conditions under which cross-lagged effects in the RI-CLPM are robust against the omission of covariate processes and the extent of this robustness.

249. Tough day ahead? The role of morning reattachment in dealing with anticipated job demands
Anna Luca Mackenbach | Goethe-Universität Frankfurt | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Anna Luca Mackenbach | Goethe-Universität Frankfurt | Germany
Malte Roswag | Universität Hildesheim
Jana Kühnel | Goethe-Universität Frankfurt

Background: Psychological reattachment refers to mentally reconnecting with one’s work before or upon returning to work. Previous research has linked reattachment to favorable outcomes, including work engagement, proactivity, and goal progress. We extend this research by investigating on which days reattachment matters most. We propose that reattachment is particularly critical on days when employees anticipate high job demands, such as heavy workload, complex tasks, and difficult social interactions. On such days, high morning reattachment should help employees better recognize their resource needs and mobilize resources accordingly. In particular, employees may engage in proactive vitality management (e.g., mobilizing energy and ensuring task focus), enact social support (e.g. seeking advice from colleagues), and enact autonomy (e.g., reordering tasks). These behaviors should ultimately make it more likely that employees attain their current workday’s goals.
Method: We are conducting a daily diary study over 10 workdays. Participants complete two questionnaires per day, one at the beginning of work and one after work. The beginning-of-work questionnaire assesses reattachment, while the after-work questionnaire captures anticipated job demands for the next day (workload, complexity, and difficult social interactions), proactive vitality management, enactment of social support, enactment of autonomy, and goal attainment. Data collection will be completed in spring 2026.
Results: Results will be available at the time of the conference.
Conclusion: Our preregistered study examines how reattachment helps employees adapt to daily work demands by enabling the mobilization of resources across the workday. Findings could inform how employees can effectively navigate workdays they anticipated to be demanding.

250. Enhancing Social Skills Through Practice: Effects and Mechanisms of a 4-Week Behavioral Intervention Study
Sarah Lindfeld | University of Münster | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Sarah Lindfeld | University of Münster | Germany
Simon M. Breil | University of Münster | Germany
Niclas Kuper | University of Münster | Germany
Mitja Back | University of Münster | Germany
Lara Kroencke | University of Münster | Germany

Social skills can be learned and improved through targeted practice. Yet most existing interventions focus on children, adolescents, or group-based settings. Evidence for individual interventions targeting social skills in adulthood remains limited. The present study investigates the effectiveness and underlying mechanisms of a four-week social behavioral intervention designed to enhance assertiveness, sociability, and warmth in adults. Using a randomized controlled trial, participants were assigned to one of three domain-specific intervention groups (i. e., assertiveness, sociability, or warmth), an active control group, or a passive control group. The intervention consisted of daily behavioral challenges which encouraged participants to practice domain-specific social behaviors in everyday life. Social skill self-concepts were assessed using the BESSI-G at pre-test and post-test. The analyses will follow three steps: First, we will investigate main effects of the intervention on social skill self-concepts. Second, we will test whether daily perceived social behavior mediates intervention effects on social skill self-concepts using multilevel structural equation modeling. This analysis will provide crucial insights into the mechanisms of change. Third, we will examine whether intervention effects are moderated by motivational variables (i.e., motivation to change, perceived ability to change) and behavioral variables (i.e., difficulty and amount of completed challenges). Together, this study provides insights into whether social skills can be effectively trained in daily life and clarifies motivational and behavioral mechanisms underlying social skill change. In addition, we will discuss how the intervention can be refined in the future, for example by increasing task difficulty.

251. Aktuelle Entwicklungen der (psycho-)gerontologischen Aus- und Weiterbildung an deutschen Hochschulen
Ann-Kristin Reinhard | Universitätsmedizin Greifswald, Institut für Community Medicine | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Ann-Kristin Reinhard | Universitätsmedizin Greifswald, Institut für Community Medicine | Germany
Eva Irene Fechau | MSB Medical School Berlin, Hochschule für Gesundheit und Medizin
Neele Grap
Prof. Dr. Eva-Marie Kessler | MSB Medical School Berlin, Hochschule für Gesundheit und Medizin
Prof. Dr. Susanne Wurm | Universitätsmedizin Greifswald, Institut für Community Medicine | Germany

Angesichts des demografischen Wandels haben gerontologische Themen zunehmende gesellschaftliche Relevanz. Während die geburtenstarken Jahrgänge in den kommenden Jahren die Regelaltersgrenze erreichen, vollzieht sich parallel ein Umbau der gerontologischen Studiengangslandschaft in Deutschland. Nach dem Ausbau eigenständiger gerontologischer Studiengänge deuten aktuelle Entwicklungen auf Diversifizierung und Rückgang dieser Angebote hin. Gleichzeitig erfolgt eine Umstrukturierung der Psychologie-Studiengänge, die eine neue Verankerung gerontologischer Inhalte zumindest im psychotherapeutischen Bereich bedeuten könnte.
Die aktuelle Studie untersucht vor diesem Hintergrund, aufbauend auf vergangenen Publikationen, die Entwicklung (psycho-)gerontologischer Studiengänge in Deutschland anhand von zwei Fragestellungen: (1) Wie haben sich grundständige und konsekutive Studiengänge in der Gerontologie seit der Bologna-Reform verändert? (2) Inwieweit sind gerontologische Inhalte in den Modulhandbüchern des neuen klinischen Psychologie-Studiengangs verankert?
Vorläufige Ergebnisse zeigen, dass gerontologische Ausbildungspfade bislang nur gering standardisiert und auf dem Arbeitsmarkt wenig sichtbar sind. Aufbauend auf einem stabilen Fundament etablierter Studiengänge zeigt sich eine Fluktuation, die durch abnehmende Studiengänge an Hochschulen für angewandte Wissenschaft sowie zunehmende Angebote an Fernhochschulen charakterisiert ist. Darüber hinaus zeichnet sich in den Modulhandbüchern der neuen klinischen Psychologie-Masterstudiengänge ab, dass gerontologische Aspekte in diesen zwar verankert sind, jedoch teilweise durch unspezifische Formulierungen unklar bleibt, inwiefern gerontologische Inhalte tatsächlich gelehrt werden.
Diese Ergebnisse stehen im Kontrast zum wachsenden Bedarf an interdisziplinär qualifizierten Fachkräften mit gerontologischer, gerontopsychologischer bzw. gerontopsychotherapeutischer Expertise. Das Projekt liefert damit wichtige Anknüpfungspunkte für Wissenschaft, Praxis und Bildungspolitik und möchte einen Beitrag zur Diskussion über notwendige strukturelle Reformen und Förderungen in der Aus- und Weiterbildung leisten. Diese Untersuchung wird im Rahmen des Peer-Mentoring Tandem-Programms der Fachgruppe Gesundheitspsychologie gefördert.

252. A Cognitive-Ecological Account of Valence Asymmetries in Attitudinal Ambivalence
Celine Frank | University of Cologne | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Celine Frank | University of Cologne | Germany
Dr. Moritz Ingendahl | Ruhr-University Bochum | Germany
Claudine Pulm | University of Cologne | Germany
Prof. Dr. Anne Gast | University of Cologne | Germany
Prof. Dr. Angela R. Dorrough | FernUniversität in Hagen | Germany
Hans Alves | Ruhr-University Bochum | Germany
Iris K. Schneider | University of Cologne / TU Dresden

Attitudinal ambivalence, the co-occurrence of positive and negative evaluations toward the same attitude object, is a common phenomenon, yet its emergence is not fully understood. Previous research has demonstrated a negativity bias in ambivalence, suggesting that negative information contributes more strongly to its emergence than positive information. We argue that this pattern does not reflect a general dominance of negative valence. Instead, drawing on a cognitive-ecological perspective, we propose that the relative similarity of positive and negative information in the evaluative environment determines their impact on ambivalence. In our first study, we find that prior evidence for a negativity bias was obtained in a negative-distinct information ecology, in which positive information was relatively similar, whereas negative information was more distinct. We therefore predict that a negativity bias will emerge specifically under such conditions. Crucially, we further predict that when the structure of the information ecology is reversed, creating a positive-distinct ecology in which negative information is more similar than positive information, a positivity bias in the emergence of ambivalence will be observed. To test these predictions, we replicate and extend previous experimental work by systematically manipulating the similarity of positive and negative evaluative information. This approach allows us to disentangle the effects of valence from the structure of the evaluative context. Overall, the present research aims to specify how characteristics of the information environment shape ambivalence, thereby contributing to a more precise understanding of when and why ambivalence arises.

253. Arbeiten mit chronischer Erkrankung?! Forschungsbasierte digitale Handlungshilfe für Beschäftigte und Unternehmen
Prof. Dr. Mathilde Niehaus | University of Cologne | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Prof. Dr. Mathilde Niehaus | University of Cologne | Germany
Dr. Marie Heide | University of Cologne | Germany
Carlotta Grupe | University of Cologne | Germany
Dr. Kathrin Staufenbiel | University of Cologne | Germany

Hintergrund:
Menschen mit chronischen Erkrankungen stehen im Arbeitsalltag häufig vor der Entscheidung, trotz gesundheitlicher Beschwerden zu arbeiten oder sich krankzumelden. Diese Entscheidungen erfordern ausgeprägte Selbstregulations- und Abwägungskompetenzen und werden durch organisationale sowie psychosoziale Faktoren wie Unterstützung oder Stigmatisierung beeinflusst. Das Projekt Amichro (2023–2026), durchgeführt in Kooperation mit der Bundesarbeitsgemeinschaft Selbsthilfe e.V., untersucht diese Prozesse empirisch mit dem Ziel, einen praxisnahen digitalen Support für Beschäftigte mit chronischer Erkrankung sowie für betriebliche Akteur*innen zu entwickeln.
Methode:
Eine systematische Literaturrecherche bündelt aktuelle Erkenntnisse zu Präsentismus, Krankheitsbewältigung und organisationalem Gesundheitsverhalten (Schmitz, Braun & Niehaus 2024). Ergänzend wurde im März 2025 eine Online-Befragung von 1.175 Erwerbstätigen mit chronischer Erkrankung durchgeführt, die Gesundheit, Leistungsfähigkeit, Präsentismus sowie arbeitsbezogene Ressourcen erfasste.
Ergebnisse:
Die Befunde bestätigen, dass Präsentismus häufig Ausdruck einer hohen Teilhabemotivation ist, jedoch mit erhöhter Erschöpfung und reduzierter Selbstfürsorge einhergehen kann. Die Entscheidungsprozesse werden durch individuelle Gesundheitsabwägungen, unterstützende Arbeitsbedingungen und verfügbare Ressourcen beeinflusst. Auf Basis dieser Erkenntnisse wurde ein digitales kostenfreies Angebot entwickelt (www.arbeiten-jaodernein.de), das durch wissenschaftlich basierte Texte (z.B. Mein Arbeitsalltag gestalten, Mein täglicher Balanceakt, Mich wertschätzen, Schritt für Schritt ins Handeln kommen) sowie praxisnahe Übungen zur gesundheitsförderlichen Selbstreflexion beiträgt. Ergänzende Informationsmodule richten sich an Akteure aus Unternehmen wie Führungskräfte, Kolleg*innen, Interessenvertretungen und an Personalabteilungen.
Fazit:
Arbeits- und gesundheitspsychologische Erkenntnisse zu Präsentismus und stay at work sind in ein anwendungsnahes digitales Werkzeug (www.arbeiten-jaodernein.de) transferiert. Das Instrument leistet einen Beitrag zur Förderung gesundheitssensibler Arbeitsgestaltung, Teilhabe und inklusiver Organisationskulturen

254. Measuring Ambivalence of Affective Normative Words Using Dual Range Sliders
Dr. Matthias Kloft | Leibnitz Institute for Educational Trajectories | Germany
Show details
Author:
Dr. Matthias Kloft | Leibnitz Institute for Educational Trajectories | Germany

Affective normative words like “fire” or “hospital” are used as stimuli in research on emotion and attention. The normative valence ratings for these words were initially collected using a bipolar rating scale from negative to positive. This comes with the challenge that neutral valence ratings on the center of the scale might mask ambivalence instead of indicating true neutrality. For example, the word "fire" can evoke both positive (bond fire) and negative (forest fire) associations for a respondent. Prior studies have investigated ambivalence by employing distinct rating scales for positive and negative valence. We propose an alternative method, namely using interval ratings on a bipolar scale collected via the dual range slider response format, where respondents can set a lower and upper bound for the valence from negative to positive. In a study involving psychology students, we demonstrate that interval ratings are effective in measuring the ambivalence of affective normative words, comparable to distinct unipolar scales.

Dr. Kristian Kleinke | University of Siegen | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Laura Cramer | University of Siegen | Germany
Dr. Kristian Kleinke | University of Siegen | Germany

This simulation study examines multiple imputation (MI) performance, with a focus on the estimation of conditional indirect effects. In the social sciences, mediation and moderated mediation analyses are frequently used, yet their results are particularly vulnerable to distortions introduced by missing data. Consequently, the choice of imputation method and model is not trivial. Two MI approaches were compared: Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE) and Multiple Imputation with Extreme Gradient Boosting (MIXGB). Large, structurally linear datasets were generated with known mechanisms to evaluate imputation performance, uncertainty estimation, and computational characteristics. Three models from Hayes (2013) were used for the simulation process: a simple mediation model (Model 4), a moderated mediation model (Model 14), and a model with double moderation of the indirect effect (Model 18). Missing values were subsequently introduced under a Missing At Random (MAR) mechanism (Rubin, 1987). Imputation performance was assessed using absolute percent bias, coverage rates, and variance-based indicators, including total and between-imputation variance and the fraction of missing information. Results indicate that MICE (function mice.impute.pmm) reliably reflects imputation uncertainty, yielding wider but more accurate confidence intervals. However, systematic instability emerged when imputing interaction terms. In contrast, MIXGB consistently underestimated between-imputation variance, resulting in overly narrow and biased confidence intervals, particularly under higher missingness rates and very large sample sizes. These findings indicate that increased algorithmic complexity and larger datasets do not inherently improve imputation quality. Instead, effective MI requires alignment between data structure, model assumptions, and the computational properties of the imputation method.

256. Wer lesen kann, kann auch schreiben – oder umgekehrt? Zur reziproken Abhängigkeit der Entwicklung der Lese- und Rechtschreibfähigkeit in der Grundschule
Jan Retelsdorf | Universität Hamburg | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Jan Retelsdorf | Universität Hamburg | Germany
Nadine Cruz Neri | Germany
Barabara Lang | Germany
Astrid Müller | Germany
Melanie Bangel | Germany

Der Erwerb grundlegender Fähigkeiten zum Lesen und Rechtschreiben stellt eine wichtige Aufgabe in der Grundschule dar. Dabei liegt bereits einige Evidenz für enge und auch wechselseitige Zusammenhänge zwischen beiden Fähigkeiten vor. Ein Großteil dieser Befunde bezieht sich durch den Fokus auf die englische Sprache auf intransparente Orthografien. In transparenteren Orthografien wie dem Deutschen können diese Zusammenhänge ganz anders aussehen. In der vorliegenden Untersuchung sollen daher für die deutsche Sprache reziproke Effekte zwischen den Entwicklungen von Lese- und Rechtschreibfähigkeiten zu Beginn der Grundschulzeit als besonders sensible Phase untersucht werden.
In der vorliegenden Studie haben wir an einer Stichprobe von insgesamt N = 523 Schüler:innen wechselseitige Beziehungen zwischen Lese- und Rechtschreibfähigkeit über drei Messzeitpunkte im Abstand von jeweils etwa 4 Monaten von Mitte der ersten Klasse bis Anfang der zweiten Klasse anhand eines Cross-Lagged-Panel Modells geschätzt. Zuvor, zu Beginn der ersten Klasse, wurden zudem das Geschlecht, das Alter, die Familiensprache, der sozioökonomische Status und die phonologische Bewusstheit der Kinder als Kovariaten erfasst. Lesefähigkeit wurde mittels Wortverständnistest aus ELFE-II, die Rechtschreibfähigkeit mittels SCHNABEL-Test erfasst. Es zeigten sich substanzielle Korrelationen nullter Ordnung zwischen beiden Fähigkeiten innerhalb der Messzeitpunkte sowie über diese hinweg. Im Cross-Lagged-Panel Modell zeigten sich signifikante Pfade der Rechtschreib- auf die Lesefähigkeit, aber nicht umgekehrt. Die Befunde werden in ihrer Bedeutung für den Lese- und Rechtschreiberwerb diskutiert.

257. Reduktion der Effekte von akustischen Störungen in einem kognitiven Leistungstests durch rosa Rauschen
Stefanie Grünewald | Institut für Präventivmedizin der Bundeswehr | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Stefanie Grünewald | Institut für Präventivmedizin der Bundeswehr | Germany
Jürgen-Philipp Rocky Spieske
Dr. Alexander Witzki | Institut für Präventivmedizin der Bundeswehr | Germany

Die Erhebung von kognitiven Leistungsdaten in der Feldforschung ist anfällig für akustische Störungen durch Lärm, Stimmen und Umweltgeräusche. Diese können gravierende Auswirkungen auf einzelne Werte haben und im schlimmsten Fall die Gesamtergebnisse von Untersuchungen beeinflussen. Ziel der vorliegenden Studie war es, die Auswirkungen von akustischen Störungen auf die Leistung in einem weit verbreiteten kognitiven Test zu quantifizieren und zu prüfen, inwieweit sich die gemessenen Störeffekte mittels des Einspielens von rosa Rauschen (1/f Rauschen) reduzieren lassen. In einem balancierten zweifaktoriellen Design absolvierten 74 Personen einem computerbasierten Arbeitsgedächtnistest (Zahlenspanne rückwärts) in vier verschiedenen Bedingungen (mit/ohne rosa Rauschen und mit/ohne akustische Störung). Es zeigten sich die erwarteten Effekte der akustischen Störung (schlechtere Leistung bei Störung) und rosa Rauschen (bessere Leistung mit rosa Rauschen). Die Interaktion von akustischer Störung und rosa Rauschen wurde in dieser Studie nicht signifikant. Es konnte jedoch auch kein signifikanter Unterschied zwischen der Kontrollbedingung ohne Störungen und ohne rosa Rauschen und der Experimentalbedingung mit Störungen und mit rosa Rauschen nachgewiesen werden. Zusammenfassend lässt sich konstatieren, dass durch akustische Störungen verursachten Leistungseinbußen in kognitiven Testverfahren durch rosa Rauschen reduziert werden können.

258. Computergestützte Erfassung von Konzentration und exekutiver Kontrolle: Evaluation einer Neuimplementierung des TEMEKKO
Stefanie Grünewald | Institut für Präventivmedizin der Bundeswehr | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Stefanie Grünewald | Institut für Präventivmedizin der Bundeswehr | Germany
Berthold Könemann
Dr. Ursa Nagler-Nitzschner | Germany
Dr. Alexander Witzki

Konzentration und exekutive Kontrolle sind zentral für kognitive Leistung und die erfolgreiche Bewältigung des Alltags. Um die Erfassung dieser Konstrukte im Rahmen von Feldforschung zu ermöglichen, wurde der numerische Teil des von Bühner und Schmidt-Atzert als papierbasiertes, psychologisches Testverfahren entwickelten und von Schmid (2010) validierten Tests zur Messung exekutiver Kontrolle / Konzentration (TEMEKKO) für die Nutzung mittels eines Tablet-Computers adaptiert und mit automatischer Itemgenerierung implementiert. In der vorliegenden Evaluationsstudie (Retest-Design, N=62) wurde neben der Reliabilität und der Konstruktvalidität (Vergleich mit d2) auch die Arbeitsbelastung im Vergleich zum d2 (NASA Task Load Index) ermittelt. Im Ergebnis zeigt sich, dass die adaptierte Fassung des TEMEKKO reliabel und valide ist. Die Einschätzung der Arbeitsbelastung durch das neue Testverfahren ergab im Vergleich zum d2 keine Unterschiede hinsichtlich der Dimensionen Geistige Anforderungen, Körperliche Anforderungen, Anstrengung, Leistung und Frustration. Lediglich der Zeitdruck wurde beim d2 signifikant höher eingeschätzt. Dieser Unterschied entsprach den Erwartungen, da bei der Bearbeitung des d2 regelmäßige Unterbrechungen aufgrund erzwungener Zeilenwechsel erfolgen. Die Bearbeitung des TEMEKKO erfolgt dagegen sowohl in der adaptierten als auch in der papierbasierten Version ohne Unterbrechung durch den Testleitenden. Zeitdruck wird stattdessen durch eine Begrenzung der Testzeit erzeugt und indem die Anzahl der Items so ausgelegt ist, dass eine vollständige Bearbeitung innerhalb dieser begrenzten Testzeit nicht möglich ist. Insgesamt ist die hier evaluierte adaptierte Fassung des TEMEKKO ein geeignetes Messinstrument, um in (Feld-)Studien Konzentration und exekutive Kontrolle zu untersuchen.

259. Theory of mind deficits in patients with behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia – using the Basel version of the Awareness of Social Inference Test – Theory of Mind
Steven Wezel | University Center for Medicine of Aging FELIX PLATTER | Switzerland
Show details

Steven Wezel | University Center for Medicine of Aging FELIX PLATTER | Switzerland
Dr. Christoph Linnemann | University Psychiatric Clinic | Switzerland
Prof. Dr. Manfred Berres | University of Applied Sciences Koblenz | Germany
Prof. Dr. Marc Sollberger | University Center for Medicine of Aging FELIX PLATTER | Switzerland

Background: Impairments in theory of mind (ToM) abilities can be observed in a range of neurodegenerative and psychiatric disorders, with varying degrees of severity. Patients with behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) exhibit severe ToM deficits even at the mild stage, whereas those with major depressive disorder (MDD), with whom they are often misdiagnosed, tend to show mild ToM deficits. Accordingly, assessing ToM capacity may help to differentiate between mild-stage bvFTD and MDD. To this end, we used the Basel version of the Awareness of Social Inference Test – Theory of Mind (BASIT-ToM), a psychometrically validated video-based test for adults with cognitive disorders that depicts naturalistic social interactions.

Methods: We administered the BASIT-ToM to seven patients with mild stage bvFTD, 21 patients with MDD and 28 patients with mild stage typical ADD, who served as positive controls for bvFTD, as also to 216 cognitively and mentally healthy subjects. In addition to the total ToM score, we calculated scores for different types of ToM, such as cognitive ToM and affective ToM, in honest and sarcastic exchanges, as also hypermentalisation.

Results: All patient groups exhibited some degree of impairment in their ToM abilities; however, these impairments varied depending on the type of ToM. Generally, patients with bvFTD demonstrated more severe ToM deficits than those with MDD or ADD.

Discussion: Our preliminary findings support the importance of ToM assessment in clinical routine for differential diagnosis of bvFTD. The subsequent implications of specific ToM subtypes will be discussed.

260. KLARpsy: Transferring research on science communication into practice
Dr. Anita Chasiotis | Leibniz-Institute for Psychology (ZPID) | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Dr. Anita Chasiotis | Leibniz-Institute for Psychology (ZPID) | Germany
Dr. Marlene Bodemer | Leibniz-Institute for Psychology (ZPID) | Germany
Dr. Martin Kerwer | Leibniz-Institute for Psychology (ZPID) | Germany

How can psychological research findings be communicated to non-expert audiences in an empirically validated way?
KLARpsy is an online platform that provides German plain-language summaries of psychological meta-analyses. It builds on extensive research conducted in the project PLan Psy (2020–2022), whose central outcome was an empirically validated writing guideline. Based on seven experimental and qualitative studies, the openly available KLARpsy guideline comprises 37 criteria addressing content, form, and presentation of plain-language summaries. Since the platform’s launch in October 2023, more than 200 summaries have been published following this guideline.
From the outset, KLARpsy has been developed as a participatory science communication project. Qualitative studies and continuous user feedback revealed heterogeneous user needs that could not be fully addressed by a single summary format: while some users expressed a need for more background information and contextualization, others perceived the texts as too extensive.
To better address these diverging needs, KLARpsy has expanded its communication formats since 2024, with a special focus on Social Media. In this context, we developed the new format Psychology Applied, which allows us to provide relevant background information to key findings. The format complements the existing platform content and is explicitly informed by prior user feedback and qualitative insights.
The poster provides an overview of how KLARpsy transfers research findings on science communication into practice, with a particular focus on newest developments. We further outline our key learnings in establishing KLARpsy as a participatory, multi-channel science communication platform.

261. A Novel Task in Exteroception Research: Electric Field Detection and Interoceptive Sensibility
Louis Papstein | Uniklinik RWTH Aachen University | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Louis Papstein | Uniklinik RWTH Aachen University | Germany
Dr. Kathrin Jankowiak | Uniklinik RWTH Aachen University | Germany
Prof. Dr. Andrea Kaifie | Uniklinik RWTH Aachen University | Germany
Prof. Dr. Thomas Kraus | Uniklinik RWTH Aachen University | Germany
Dr. Michael Kursawe | Uniklinik RWTH Aachen University | Germany

The relationship between interoception, the perception of internal bodily signals, and exteroception, the perception of external stimuli, remains contested. Recent work suggests that interoceptive sensibility (IS), the subjective capacity for interoception, can lead to a response bias in exteroception, increasing false alarms. Simultaneously, the link between IS and exteroception is unclear. Electric fields (EF) are ubiquitous in modern environments and can be used as novel exteroceptive stimulus in experimental settings. This study investigates whether IS predicts EF detection ability and response bias to refine the conceptualization of interoception and advance understanding of EF perception.
A secondary analysis of an EF exposure study with 203 healthy adults (20–79 years) was conducted. Whole-body exposure included alternating current, direct current, and hybrid EFs. Sensitivity (d′) and response criterion (c) were computed from hit and false alarm rates. IS was assessed with the Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness (MAIA).
Multiple regression analyses, using the eight MAIA subscales as predictors, showed no significant associations with detection performance [F(8,194) = 1.097, p = 0.367] or response bias [F(8,194) = 0.883, p = 0.532].
Contrary to our hypothesis, IS did not predict response bias in EF perception and was not a significant predictor of detection performance, but the results did indicate a non-significant trend for two subscales of the MAIA. One reason for the null effect could be the unfamiliarity of the exteroceptive stimulus. Future studies should integrate objective interoception measures and assess the effect of task familiarity.

262. Neuroticism Facets and Relationship Satisfaction in Couples: Evidence From Dyadic Data
Prof. Dr. Swetlana Wildfang | Europäische Fernhochschule Hamburg | Germany
Show details
Author:
Prof. Dr. Swetlana Wildfang | Europäische Fernhochschule Hamburg | Germany

A negative association between neuroticism and relationship satisfaction is well established in relationship research. However, most previous studies have examined neuroticism as a global personality factor, whereas the role of specific neuroticism facets and dyadic interdependencies has received considerably less attention. The present study therefore adopted a facet-level approach to neuroticism as conceptualized in the Big Five Inventory–2 (BFI-2; Christopher J. Soto & Oliver P. John, 2017) and investigated associations between the facets anxiety, depression, and emotional volatility and relationship satisfaction in heterosexual couples, with a particular focus on actor and partner effects.

The sample comprised 87 heterosexual couples who completed a standardized questionnaire including selected scales of the BFI-2. Dyadic associations were analyzed using the Actor–Partner Interdependence Model.

Results indicated a significant negative association between depression and women’s own relationship satisfaction. Among men, anxiety was significantly negatively related to their own relationship satisfaction. Furthermore, the neuroticism facet emotional volatility showed significant negative actor and partner effects among men, suggesting reciprocal influences within the dyad.

These findings underscore the value of a facet-level approach to neuroticism in relationship research. In particular, the results highlight gender-specific patterns and dyadic interdependencies that remain obscured when neuroticism is assessed as a global trait. Differentiating between anxiety, depressive affect, and emotional volatility contributes to a more nuanced understanding of relationship functioning and offers relevant implications for couple counseling and psychotherapy.

263. PRICE TRANSPARENCY – Effects on Consumer Trust in E-Commerce Contexts
Matthias Müller | Technische Hochschule Ingolstadt (THI) | Germany
Show details
Authors:

Vanessa Gabriela Yarza Navarro-Schär | Ludwig-Maximilian-Universität München (LMU) | Germany
Prof. Dr. Eric Eller | Technische Hochschule Ingolstadt (THI) | Germany
Prof. Dr. Christine Hennighausen | Technische Hochschule Ingolstadt (THI) | Germany

Customer trust is a key driver of loyalty in e-commerce, yet empirical evidence on how price transparency shapes trust remains mixed. This thesis examines how different levels of price disclosure affect consumer trust and the trustworthiness dimensions ability, benevolence and integrity. In a fictional shopping scenario, N = 259 participants viewed an online fashion store presenting two products, a cashmere sweater and a cotton T-shirt. Each product was randomly assigned to one of three experimental conditions: high price transparency (detailed cost breakdown), low price transparency (disclosure of total manufacturing costs), or a control condition (only the price was shown). The results indicate that high price transparency significantly increases customer trust in the online store, with the effect observed consistently across both products. The strongest and most consistent effects are found for perceived integrity. For both products, high and low transparency are significant compared with the control condition. For perceived ability, high transparency shows significant increases, while low transparency is not significant. For perceived benevolence, high transparency is significant for the T-shirt and shows a statistical trend for the sweater. Price fairness and involvement are positive predictors of trust. Overall, the study establishes a theoretically grounded link between price transparency and trust dimensions and demonstrates that transparent price communication can serve as an effective tool to foster customer trust in e-commerce, provided that its design is aligned with product characteristics.

Das Hamburger Führungsmotivationsinventar (FÜMO) wurde im Zeitraum von 2009 bis 2012 entwickelt. Es handelt sich um ein Instrument zur gendersensitiven Erfassung von Führungsmotivation, welches aus intrapersoneller Perspektive einen Beitrag leistet, um die weiterhin bestehende Unterrepräsentanz von Frauen in Führungspositionen zu beleuchten. In Anlehnung an die von Chan und Drasgow (2001) vorgeschlagenen Dimensionen – affektive, normative und kalkulative Führungsmotivation – steht ein differenziertes Fragebogeninstrument zur Verfügung, welches seit 2014 zur Beratung und zum Coaching von (potentiellen) Führungskräften genutzt wird.
In der aktuellen Studie wird nach über 14 Jahren erstmals die langfristige prognostische Validität des Instruments geprüft. Über 1100 Teilnehmer*innen aus den Konstruktions- und Validierungsstudien wurden kontaktiert und bezüglich ihrer beruflichen Entwicklung befragt. Ein Matching der Daten mit den Antworten zu den Dimensionen der Führungsmotivation von vor 14-17 Jahren soll Aufschluss geben, ob Personen mit einer höheren Führungsmotivation im späteren Berufsverlauf auch eher eine Führungsposition eingenommen haben, ggf. eine höhere Führungsebene im Unternehmen erreicht haben, ein höheres Gehalt bekommen und/oder durchgängig in Führungspositionen tätig waren.

265. Including Strengths or Excluding Flaws? The Impact of Screening Strategies on Online Dating
Sophie Katharina Doege | Universität Salzburg | Austria
Show details
Authors:
Jochim Hansen | Universität Salzburg | Austria
Sophie Katharina Doege | Universität Salzburg | Austria
Mai A. T. Tran

Online dating platforms require judgments based on limited profile information. We investigated whether seeking strengths (i.e., an inclusion strategy) versus overlooking flaws (i.e., an exclusion strategy) produces different evaluations of individual profiles, and whether effects can be explained by the size of the attribute set used to represent the target. In an online experiment, participants (N = 377) were randomly assigned to evaluate eight fictitious dating profiles using either an inclusion strategy (identifying positive attributes) or an exclusion strategy (delete undesirable attributes). After each profile, participants rated interpersonal attraction, perceived shared reality, and intention to meet. Linear mixed-effects models showed that exclusion (vs. inclusion) yielded more favorable evaluations across outcomes. Causal mediation analyses indicated robust positive indirect effects of strategy via set size on all outcome variables, while direct effects of strategy (controlling for set size) were negative, consistent with associative activation from focusing on undesirable versus desirable attributes. Thus, exclusion led to more positive overall evaluations because it preserved a broader set of (primarily positive and neutral) attributes, wiping out the effect of its evaluative focus per se. The findings extend inclusion–exclusion theory from multi-option choice to single-target evaluation and suggest practical implications for early-stage screening on dating platforms: broader, less restrictive exclusion-based processing may increase initial interest, potentially expanding opportunities for subsequent offline assessment.

266. Modern payment systems and consumer behaviour: A biopsychological investigation of the influence of payment systems on purchasing behaviour
Marc Ritter | Hochschule für Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft Ludwigshafen | Germany

Celine Blettner | Hochschule für Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft Ludwigshafen | Germany
Prof. Dr. Gerhard Raab | Hochschule für Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft Ludwigshafen | Germany

Contemporary payment methods offer benefits to both retailers and customers (Gieselmann & Gremmer, 2018). However, the acceleration of the payment process, the accompanying decoupling and increasing lack of transparency between consumption and payment can increase willingness to spend and encourage problematic purchasing behaviour, as it becomes more difficult to control spending behaviour (Schomburgk et al., 2024; Broekhoff & Cruijsen, 2024; Ahn & Nam, 2022; Raab, 1998). In this respect aspects such as varying pain of payment, the illusion of liquidity and the associated influence on mental accounting play a decisive role. Despite the considerable research that has already been conducted on cash and credit card payments, payment methods such as mobile-payment and biometric payment and their influence on consumer behaviour remain a relatively underexplored field. Moreover, there is a paucity of diversity in the research methods employed to date (Dahlberg, 2015). The aim is therefore to investigate the influence of diverse payment systems (cash, credit card, mobile and biometric payment) on purchasing behaviour from a psychological and consumer policy perspective. To this end the study combines an experiment in the form of a department store game developed by Raab (1998), which simulates realistic shopping scenarios in analogue form, with biopsychological measurements (Affective Computing), observation and a subsequent survey to gain a holistic understanding of behavioural responses. In an initial pre-test with 20 participants, the department store game will be tested, feedback collected and then accordingly adjusted. During the conference initial findings will be presented and possible limitations discussed.

267. Evidenzorientiertes Problemlösen von Lehramtsstudierenden: Einfluss von Dokumentquelle und Passung auf die Informationsnutzung
Dr. Martin Greisel | Universität Augsburg
Show details
Authors:
Sophia Just | Universität Augsburg | Germany
Dr. Martin Greisel | Universität Augsburg
Lea C. Schwindt | Universität des Saarlandes
Prof. Dr. Robin Stark | Universität des Saarlandes
Prof. Dr. Ingo Kollar | Universität Augsburg

Konfrontiert mit der – in der Praxis oft schwierigen – Aufgabe, unterrichtliche Problemsituationen evidenzorientiert zu analysieren, können Lehramtsstudierende auf wissenschaftliche oder nicht-wissenschaftliche Dokumente zurückgreifen (Art der Quelle). Diese können entweder die Problemursachen oder deren Symptome adressieren (Art der Passung). Unklar ist, wie sich Quelle und Passung von Dokumenten darauf auswirken, wie Lehramtsstudierende enthaltene Informationen bei der Problemanalyse nutzen (RQ1) und inwiefern sie bei der Dokumentenauswahl Informationen über die Quellen berücksichtigen (Sourcing; RQ2).

N=443 Lehramtsstudierende erstellten in einem 2x2-within-subjects-Design Handlungsvorschläge zu vier Unterrichtsproblemen. Dabei konnten sie je ein wissenschaftliches und ein nicht-wissenschaftliches Dokument nutzen, die sich in ihrer Passung zum jeweiligen Unterrichtsproblem (Fokus auf Problemursache oder -symptom) unterschieden. Für die Kodierung der Informationsnutzung aus wissenschaftlichen und nicht-wissenschaftlichen Quelle wurde die Übereinstimmung einer Schlüsselwörter-basierten Kodierung mit zwei unabhängigen Kodierer*innen berechnet (Gwet’s AC1=.890-.923). Zur Messung von Sourcing erfassten wir, ob die Teilnehmenden auf Links klickten, die Hintergrundinformationen zur Quelle lieferten.

Bezüglich RQ1 wurden Dokumente aus nicht-wissenschaftlicher Quelle signifikant seltener (β=−0.10, p < .001) und Dokumente mit problemursachenbezogener Passung signifikant häufiger (β=0.35, p < .001) genutzt als wissenschaftliche oder symptombezogene Dokumente. Die Interaktion war nicht signifikant (β=−0.01, p=.484). Bezüglich RQ2 zeigte sich, dass mehr Sourcing betrieben wurde, wenn beide Dokumente gleich passend waren, als wenn eines ursachen- und eines symptombezogen passte (β=0.16, p < .001).

Lehramtsstudierende scheinen bei unterrichtlichen Problemanalysen überraschenderweise wissenschaftliche gegenüber nicht-wissenschaftlichen Dokumenten zu bevorzugen und ursachenbezogene Problemlösestrategien als überlegen erkennen zu können (RQ1). Zusätzlich scheinen sie insbesondere dann Sourcing zu betreiben (RQ2), wenn sie Inkohärenzen zwischen Dokumenten nicht inhaltlich lösen können.

Awe is a phenomenon that is reported in connection with extraordinary experiences and has been frequently investigated since the early 2000s. The Awe Experience Scale Short Form (AWE-SF; Graziosi et al., 2024) is a widely applied tool for assessing awe, comprising six subscales. We aimed to expand on previous quantitative research on the quality criteria of the AWE-SF with a mixed-methods design to investigate how well participants' perspectives (mostly laypeople) matched those of researchers. In two studies with 33 US-American citizens (Study 1: Written interview, n = 22; Study 2: Oral interview, n = 11), we investigated how participants’ interpretations and researchers’ definitions of the AWE-SF were aligned. Additionally, we analyzed how well participants’ item interpretations represented their conceptualization of awe. In both studies, participants were asked to report on their awe conceptualizations, their latest awe experience, their perceptions of each of the AWE-SF items and to rate their agreement with the items. Although some item interpretations matched with researchers’ definitions, qualitative content analysis revealed that participants in both studies had issues to interpret and report on items among several subscales. Across all subscales, item interpretations diverged from respective subscale definitions and in some cases even aligned better with a different subscale definition. Generally, the AWE-SF appeared to be missing crucial facets to adequately assess participants’ awe conceptualization. Mixed-methods analysis revealed that quantitative ratings only poorly reflected the qualitative reports on awe experiences. Based on our findings, we derive suggestions to improve the AWE-SF to increase clarity in awe research.

Nele Reinsberg | MSH Medical School Hamburg - University of Applied Sciences and Medical University | Germany

Prof. Dr. habil. Anett Müller-Alcazar | MSH Medical School Hamburg - University of Applied Sciences and Medical University | Germany

Loneliness and perceived social isolation are highly prevalent, particularly during the recent COVID-19 pandemic. Loneliness can result from social exclusion; both can have profound effects on mental and physical health, being associated with diseases such as depression, migraine and acute or chronic pain. Previous studies indicate that social exclusion and physical pain activate similar brain regions, suggesting a neural overlap between social and physical pain systems. However, as the relationship between social exclusion and pain perception remains unclear, our study aims to investigate this experimentally, building on the work of Eisenberger et al. (2003). With data collection ongoing, n = 78 healthy participants underwent the Cyberball paradigm so far, a virtual ball tossing-game for the experimental induction of social exclusion. Participants’ wellbeing (e.g., pain and stress perception) was assessed using questionnaires. Moreover, physiological markers such as heart rate and heart rate variability (subsample of n = 28) were measured. Preliminary results indicate that social exclusion was successfully induced in our sample: Participants reported significantly higher levels of perceived exclusion and rejection (p ≤ .001), as well as stress (p ≤ .01) following exclusion versus inclusion. Only non-significant descriptive tendencies have been observed in relation to pain ratings so far. Further results on the impact of social exclusion on stress and pain perception will be discussed. Given the high prevalence of loneliness and pain, this pilot study provides valuable insights into social exclusion and its health implications, which could contribute to shaping future preventive and treatment efforts, especially for pain disorders.

Children’s books are discussed as an important source for the acquisition and reinforcement of gender stereotypes, but also as a potential means to challenge them. This study examined the influence of counter-stereotypical short stories on children’s gender stereotypes and their behavioural intentions toward gender-typed activities. We investigated whether effects differed between preschool and elementary school children and whether gender typicality of the story’s protagonist moderated effects of counter-stereotypical stories.
149 children (75 female) participated in the study, including 97 preschool children (3–6 years) and 52 elementary school children (9–11 years). Children listened to 32 counter-stereotypical short stories. Each story depicted a gender-stereotypical activity performed by a counter-stereotypical main character. The protagonist was portrayed either as gender-typical or gender-atypical. The children completed the task in a computer-based format, indicating after each story on a visual-analog scale the association with gender (ranging from only boys to only girls) as well as their behavioural intention (ranging from not at all to absolutely). Gender-association and behavioural-intention ratings for each of the gender-stereotypical activities were also collected prior to the intervention.
Preliminary results indicate that counter-stereotypical stories reduced gender-stereotypical associations, with boys showing lower stereotypes for female-typed activities and girls showing stronger effects for male-typed activities. This effect was moderated by age, with stronger reductions in primary school children than in preschool children. Behavioural intentions to engage in counter-stereotypical activities increased after story exposure, particularly in girls for male-typed activities and in primary school children. The typicality of the story character had no effect.

271. Individual differences in nocebo hyperalgesia
Dr. Marian van der Meulen | University of Luxembourg | Luxembourg
Show details
Author:
Dr. Marian van der Meulen | University of Luxembourg | Luxembourg

Placebo and nocebo effects (i.e., positive and negative treatment expectations) substantially influence pain perception. Yet, these effects vary greatly across individuals, making them challenging to utilize in treatment. We explored the role of different psychophysiological factors in modulating placebo and nocebo responsiveness, in particular, inhibitory control, pain-related cognitions and stress regulation.
58 young healthy participants were exposed to heat pain stimuli on the arm, while we manipulated expectations regarding the intensity via a sham transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) device. Participants were told that the device would either increase (nocebo condition) or decrease pain (placebo condition), although it was inactive throughout the experiment. We recorded resting heart rate variability (HRV) using electrocardiograms and pain-related cognitions through standard questionnaires. The cortisol awakening response (CAR) was assessed using saliva samples on two consecutive days prior to the laboratory session.
High frequency HRV was negatively correlated with the nocebo response, suggesting that stronger prefrontal inhibitory control may protect against expectation-driven pain amplification. Fear of pain was positively correlated with the nocebo effect. And finally, higher cortisol levels (CAR) were associated with a stronger nocebo response, implicating stress-related vulnerability to negative expectations. No correlations were observed for placebo responses.
These findings underscore the role of individual differences in inhibitory control, stress regulation, and pain-related fear in shaping nocebo effects, and point to potential targets for reducing expectation-driven adverse outcomes.

The present study investigates associations between social situation characteristics and psychological states, with an emphasis on identifying consistent contingencies and individual differences in them. Although research on situational contingencies has increased, systematic investigations of multiple social situation characteristics and corresponding behavioral and emotional states in social interactions remain scarce. We focus on contingencies emerging from theoretically expected combinations of six situation characteristics (status opportunity, interpersonal competition, positive sociality, personal exchange, affection demands, and evaluative stressors) with four states (assertiveness, sociability, warmth, and nervousness). N = 96 participants took part in a four-week experience sampling study, reporting four times daily on their social situations and their behavioral and emotional states. Multilevel models showed that (1) social situation characteristics were linked to psychological states in expected ways on average, (2) individuals differed significantly in these contingencies, and (3) preliminary moderation analyses showed no interaction effects with conceptually related personality trait self-reports. These findings contribute to a more contextual, process-based understanding of social personality. Notably, larger-scale replications of this pilot study are required, especially for sufficiently powered investigations of links between classical trait measures and contingencies.

Everyday self-control failures can often lead to adverse long-term effects on health and well-being. The motivational processes and individual differences underlying such failures provide a promising research avenue to identify risk factors and targets for health interventions. We present two studies that investigated the motivational and personality influences on the use of justifications for indulgence. The first study (N = 151) focused on testing the causal effect of cravings on endorsement of six types of justifications identified by Taylor et al. (2014). Participants were randomly assigned to either of the two conditions, a craving and a control condition. It was hypothesized that participants in the craving condition will endorse justifications more strongly than the control condition; and that higher trait self-control will predict weaker endorsement of justifications in both the conditions. While the results did not reveal any significant differences in the use of justifications in the two conditions, it was found that individuals with lower trait self-control scores endorsed deservingness and curiosity justifications more strongly compared to individuals with higher trait self-control. Further exploratory analyses revealed that the strength of cravings predicted the use of certain justifications. Based on these results, we conducted a second study (N = 271) which replicated and extended the correlational effects of individual differences on the frequency of employing justifications when indulging. Higher trait self-control predicted less frequent use of justifications, whereas controlled motivation and higher frequency of cravings predicted more frequent use of justifications.

274. Facing Reality: A Mobile-EEG-VR-Study of Face Processing and Recognition using Dynamic Virtual Avatars
Merle Sagehorn | Universität Osnabrück, Institut für Psychologie | Germany
Show details
Author:
Merle Sagehorn | Universität Osnabrück, Institut für Psychologie | Germany

Face perception in everyday social interactions unfolds under dynamic and highly realistic conditions, yet most experimental research relies on static, two-dimensional stimuli. To bridge this gap and increase ecological validity, we investigated how stimulus realism affects face encoding and recognition under immersive virtual conditions. In a mobile EEG study, participants encountered dynamic 3D virtual avatars as well as static 2D images of avatars within a shared virtual environment. Subsequently, face recognition was assessed using a 2D old/new task. Cognitive processing during encoding and retrieval was examined using event-related potentials (ERPs) and induced oscillatory activity. While cognitive load during encoding did not differ between 2D and 3D faces, recognition performance was significantly higher for faces that had been encoded as 3D avatars. Importantly, retrieval of 3D-encoded faces engaged distinct mnemonic mechanisms, as reflected in face-specific old/new effects across characteristic ERP components and frequency bands. The observed pattern suggests the joint contribution of familiarity- and recollection-based processes as well as enhanced allocation of attentional resources. Together, the findings suggest that realistic 3D faces, by virtue of their increased visual complexity and social relevance, promote the formation of stimulus-specific memory engrams that support superior recognition performance. The results highlight the importance of realism in the study of memory and social perception and underscore the value of immersive virtual environments for psychological research.

Ausgehend von rollen- und familiensystemtheoretischen Überlegungen werden Veränderungen im Karrierecommitment innerhalb von Paaren während der Transition zur Elternschaft untersucht. Karrierecommitment beschreibt die Identifikation mit der eigenen Karriere und das Interesse am beruflichen Fortkommen. Bisherige Studien haben sich meist auf die berufliche Entwicklung von Müttern fokussiert. Ein wesentlicher Beitrag dieser Studie ist die simultane Betrachtung karrierebezogener Einstellungen beider Partner, also von Mann und Frau, die sich auch gegenseitig beeinflussen könnten. Aus rollentheoretischer Sicht wurde erwartet, dass Männer ein höheres Ausgangsniveau im Karrierecommitment aufweisen als Frauen und bei ihnen das Karrierecommitment nach der Geburt nicht abnimmt, während dies bei Müttern eher anzunehmen ist. Auf der Paarebene erwarteten wir, dass das Karrierecommitment von Frauen mit überdauernd stark karriereorientiertem Partner besonders deutlich abnimmt.
Längsschnittlich wurden 373 heterosexuelle (werdende) Ersteltern-Paare während der Schwangerschaft sowie 3, 6, 12 und 18 Monate nach der Geburt befragt. Zur Datenmodellierung wurde eine Dyadic Latent Growth Curve Analysis eingesetzt. In Übereinstimmung mit rollentheoretischen Erwartungen fiel das Ausgangsniveau des Karrierecommitments der Väter höher aus als das der Mütter. Nach der Geburt kam es sowohl bei den Müttern als auch bei den Vätern zu einer signifikanten Abnahme des Karrierecommitments, ohne Geschlechtsunterschiede in der Veränderung. Zudem zeigten sich auf Paarebene keine Zusammenhänge zwischen den Ausgangswerten sowie dem Grad an Veränderung im Karrierecommitment zwischen den Beziehungspartnern. Daraus kann u.a. geschlossen werden, dass ihr Karrierecommitment sich nach der Geburt unabhängig voneinander entwickelt.

Since 2020, the “Dresdner Treffpunkt Sicherheit und Gesundheit bei der Arbeit” has been offered as a digital event series, enabling nationwide participation and sustainable knowledge in accordance with the 2016 guidelines of the German Wissen-schaftsrat for transfer activities. This web-based format, hosted by the Federal Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (BAuA), presents current research, regulatory developments, and emerging topics such as AI in occupational safety. The digital format has been offering interactive workshops, lectures, and discussions tailored to diverse stakeholders. Digital events were evaluated in 2023-2025. We analyze differ-ences in evaluation results across years to identify determinants of successful digital knowledge transfer and inform future formats.

Survey questions were aligned with three levels of the Kirkpatrick evaluation model (Kirkpatrick & Kirkpatrick, 2016): reaction, knowledge, and behavior. In 2023, knowledge level was assessed qualitatively, while results were measured in a subse-quent survey. In total, 1170 persons participated in 2023 (t1: 1122; t2: 848), 1413 persons in 2024, and 1075 persons in our evaluation survey, corresponding to ap-proximately 30% of event attendees. Differences across evaluation levels were investigated using SPSS Statistics 31.

We detected significant differences in reaction (F(22, 6728) = 6.01, p < .001) and behavior (Welch´s F(2, 2045.86) = 175.81, p < .001) across years. Furthermore, a significant increase in knowledge was observed in 2024 and 2025; however, analysis showed a significantly higher increase in 2025 (t(2288) = 3.73, p < .001). Advanced analysis will examine potential causes, such as participant numbers and event format, for the observed findings.

Situational judgment tests (SJTs) are popular and cost-effective personnel selection tools with good predictive power for job performance. At the same time, SJTs are largely based on situations conveyed through language, which raises the question of whether small linguistic variations can influence the measurement properties.
Against the backdrop of the still current controversial public and scientific debate on gender-inclusive language, it is particularly relevant to determine whether different gender formulations in test items influence the psychometric properties of tests.
In this pre-registered study, we examine whether different variants of gender-related formulations in German-language SJT items change the construct validity and whether individual differences (age, political identification, attitude toward gender-inclusive language) are related to these effects.
Participants (N = 520) complete 8 agreeableness scenarios, randomly assigned to one of four wording conditions: generic masculine, generic feminine, double form with slash, and gender asterisk. In addition, they completed a self-report on agreeableness (8 items) and a short form of the BFI-2 to test discriminant validity. As individual differences predictors, we measured attitudes toward gender-inclusive language, perceived behavioral control in gendering, political orientation, and age.
We report convergent and discriminant validities for the four versions. In addition, we use regression models to test whether the strength of the SJT-self-report correlation differs between the four conditions and separately examine whether this correlation varies depending on individual differences predictors. Implications for linguistic fairness, comparability of SJT scores, and practical testing recommendations are discussed.

Dr. Nida ul Habib Bajwa | Saarland University | Germany

Social-Engineering-Angriffe stellen eine zunehmende Bedrohung für Organisationen dar, da sie gezielt menschliche Schwachstellen ausnutzen, um an sensible Daten zu gelangen. Viele Aufklärungsmaßnahmen zielen darauf ab, Endnutzer:innen den Wert ihrer Daten im Sinne einer Kosten–Nutzen-Abwägung bewusst zu machen. Die Theorie der kontextuellen Integrität hingegen geht davon aus, dass Daten keinen absoluten Wert besitzen, sondern dass deren Weitergabe vom jeweiligen Kommunikationskontext abhängt. Vor diesem Hintergrund untersucht die vorliegende Studie, ob Kosten–Nutzen-Abwägungen von Opfern telefonischen Betrugs durch einen als passend wahrgenommenen Kontext überlagert werden. In einem 2x2-Zwischen-Versuchspersonen-Design wurden 52 Mitarbeitende der Universität des Saarlandes mit simulierten Vishing-Anrufen konfrontiert, wobei sowohl die wahrgenommenen Kosten der Datenpreisgabe als auch die kontextuelle Integrität experimentell variiert wurden. Als abhängige Variable wurde die Anzahl während des Anrufs ausgeführter sensibler Handlungen erfasst, darunter das Weitergeben eines Codes, das Einrichten einer PIN sowie das Ausführen eines vermeintlichen Diagnosetools. Die Ergebnisse zeigten weder signifikante Haupteffekte der Kosten–Nutzen-Manipulation noch der kontextuellen Integrität, ebenso wenig einen Interaktionseffekt. Auffällig war jedoch ein stark polarisiertes Entscheidungsverhalten: Rund 50 % der Teilnehmenden führten alle abgefragten Handlungen aus, während etwa 30 % keinerlei sensible Handlungen vornahmen. Explorative Analysen zeigten zudem, dass ein höheres selbsteingeschätztes IT-Wissen mit einer geringeren Bereitschaft zur Durchführung sensibler Handlungen einherging.

In a consensus statement a huge research-practicioner-gap was identified in attachment theory leading to misinterpretation and misapplication of research findings. This not only holds for child protection, where decisions might have major consequences for families, but might also be true for other practicioners, e.g., in early childhood intervention (ECI). Furthermore, even when trying to use attachment-based methods, current possibilities are too complex not suitable for everyday practice.
Therefore, the current pilot study, conducted in two rounds in 2023 and 2025 pursued two goals: (1) assessing opinions and knowledge about attachment theory among practicioners, and (2) investigating competencies in assessing parental sensitivity before and after a short video-based training.
In the study interdisciplinary professionals (N=63 in 2023; N=148 in 2025) participated in an evaluation before and 4 weeks after the training, which consisted of two online sessions in 2023 or rather an e-learning in 2025. The evaluation comprised a questionnaire on knowledge and opinions about attachment theory, and a rating of parental sensitivity and dysfunctional parental behavior in videos on parent-child-interactions.
The vast majority agreed that attachment theory is empirically well-founded and very valuable in their practical work. Knowledge varied considerably between individuals, but through the training, a significant increase in knowledge could be acchieved. In the first round in 2023, maybe also due to methodological reasons, results even indicated a decrease of correctly assigned videos. In 2025, tendentially improved ratings of sensitivity and dysfunctional behavior could be seen.
Implications of these findings for the implementation of practicioner-trainings will be discussed.

Maurits Dietrich | Ruhr-Unitversität Bochum | Germany

Prof. Dr. Marcel Kern | Georg-August-Universität Göttingen | Germany

In prior multilevel research on team functioning, scholars have primarily relied on aggregating individual team members’ survey ratings to assess emergent team states and team performance. This aggregation approach assumes that team constructs are experienced similarly by all members, such that aggregate mean values adequately represent team-level variables. Challenging this consensus-based perspective, a growing body of research suggests that within-team differences offer valuable insights into team functioning beyond those captured by average mean values alone. Accordingly, team-level dispersion metrics such as variance, skewness, and kurtosis may serve as critical indicators for identifying distinct patterns of dispersion across teams. The present study examined whether such distinct dispersion patterns can be identified for perceived team performance and for the emergent states of psychological safety climate, distributive justice, team trust, and illegitimate tasks, which represent core constructs of the stress-as-offense-to-self framework. Data were collected from 838 individuals nested within 156 real working teams across various industry sectors. Using hierarchical cluster analysis, we identified between two and four distinct dispersion patterns for each team-level variable. Across all constructs, the resulting clusters corresponded closely to dispersion patterns described in prior research, including minority belief, bimodal, fragmented, and triangular patterns (DeRue et al., 2010; Loignon et al., 2019). Taken together, these findings underscore that dispersion metrics, beyond mean levels, may play a meaningful role in capturing team-level phenomena. Future research could build on this work by examining the relationships between team-level constructs, while considering their different dispersion patterns.
