Identifying and responding to learning and behavioural difficulties in children is part of physicians’, school psychologists’, and teachers’ professional skills. However, there are few practical training opportunities, leading to insufficient acquisition of diagnostic and intervention-related skills (Poznanski et al., 2021; Bauer et al., 2022). To find effective ways of supporting skill acquisition in future professionals, it is essential to examine the knowledge bases of students across these three disciplines.

The present study will investigate the use of case simulations to assess diagnostic and intervention-related skills of university students from the three disciplines with varying specialisations and corresponding knowledge bases as part of their learning prerequisites (medical, school psychology, and teacher students, target sample based on power-analysis: N = 111). Students will work on eight multimodal digital simulated case scenarios of grade 2 pupils with varying symptoms of behavioural and learning difficulties. For each case, participants can access different information sources typically available in the school context (e.g., parent and teacher interviews, observations of behaviour, work examples). Participants will be asked to submit written responses in which they provide and justify their diagnosis and recommended interventions for each of the simulated cases. This study assesses the learning prerequisites of the three student groups in a pre-test and compares the student groups regarding their knowledge bases and their diagnostic and intervention-related skills. Data will be collected between March and May 2026 and the results will be presented at the conference.

282. Lone actor terrorism revisited: Comparative predictors and ideological heterogeneity in the United States
Anna Knorr | Germany
Show details
Author:
Anna Knorr | Germany

Lone-actor terrorism is often treated as a distinct phenomenon, yet evidence about how lone offenders differ from extremists who act within groups remains inconsistent and frequently based on small or single-ideology samples. Using a national dataset of 3,203 extremist offenders in the United States, we integrate formal statistical inference with interpretable machine-learning methods to quantify the most diagnostic predictors of lone offending relative to group-based offending. Documented indicators of mental illness are the strongest differentiator between lone and group-based offenders in open-source records, followed by lower levels of group grievance, older age, unmarried status, absence of trauma history, and weaker ideological commitment. At the same time, lone offenders are more likely to engage in violent behavior (since internet onset) and are more often motivated by issue-specific agendas rather than broader ideological frameworks, in contrast to group-based extremists. Within the lone-actor population, operational profiles also diverge markedly by ideology: Islamist lone actors exhibit the most extensive preparation and the highest fatality intent, yet the lowest odds of plot success; left-wing lone actors show the least preparation and the highest likelihood of event-triggered radicalization; right-wing lone actors have comparatively higher rates of civilian targeting and military experience. These findings refine prevailing assumptions about lone-actor terrorism and provide a stronger empirical basis for theory and prevention.

283. Toward integration: a cognitive-motivational perspective on extremism
Anna Knorr | Germany
Show details
Author:
Anna Knorr | Germany

While the ‘rigidity-of-the-extreme’ research line focuses on deficits in cognitive flexibility (CF), the Significance Quest Theory highlights the motivational quest for significance (QFS) as a central driver of radicalization. Despite calls for integration, these research lines have not been combined, nor have their effects been disentangled across different dimensions of extremism. This preregistered study examines whether an interaction between CF and QFS is associated with ideological (Nationalism), attitudinal (Willingness to Fight for the National Group), and behavioral (Political Violence) extremism. Data were analyzed from 957 Polish adolescents, an age group vulnerable to radicalization. Latent moderated structural equation modeling was employed to test the interaction of CF and QFS. Results showed that the interaction was associated with ideological and behavioral extremism and approached significance for attitudinal extremism. QFS was positively associated with ideological and attitudinal extremism at low CF but with behavioral extremism only at high CF, indicating distinct effects across extremism dimensions. This study expands the empirical body on Significance Quest Theory by demonstrating that CF moderates the relationship between QFS and extremist outcomes and illustrates how their interplay shapes different dimensions of extremism.

284. Im Spannungsfeld multipler Peer-Feedback-Nachrichten: Wie Studierende Feedback von mehreren Peers integrieren
Martin Greisel | Universität Augsburg | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Martin Greisel | Universität Augsburg | Germany
Julia Hornstein | Universität Augsburg | Germany
Ingo Kollar | Universität Augsburg | Germany

Computerunterstütztes Peer-Feedback ist eine wirksame Methode, um den Lernprozess von Studierenden zu unterstützen. Allerdings ist unklar, wie Studierende multiple Peer-Feedback-Nachrichten integrieren, wodurch unterschiedliche Integrationsmuster prädiziert werden und welche Konsequenzen diese auf den weiteren Peer-Feedback-Prozess und den Lernerfolg haben. Diese Studie untersucht deshalb, wie Studierende multiple Peer-Feedback-Nachrichten integrieren, welchen Einfluss objektive (strukturelle Feedbackqualität, Akkuratheit, Relevanz, Umsetzbarkeit) und subjektive Feedbackmerkmale (subjektive Feedbackqualität, subjektive Angemessenheit) darauf haben, wie Studierende diese integrieren und welche Auswirkungen unterschiedliche Integrationsmuster auf den weiteren Peer-Feedback-Prozess (Implementationshäufigkeit) und den Lernerfolg (Revisionsqualität, domänenspezifisches Wissen) haben. Zur Beantwortung dieser Forschungsfragen wurde eine explorative Studie mit N=100 Lehramtsstudierenden durchgeführt. Die Studierenden hatten die Aufgabe, einen authentischen Unterrichtsfall zu analysieren, zwei Peers Feedback zu geben und die beiden erhaltenen Peer-Feedback-Nachrichten miteinander zu integrieren. Zur Unterstützung und Sichtbarmachung des Integrationsprozesses erhielten die Studierenden eine Schritt-für-Schritt-Anleitung, die aus der multiplen Dokumentenforschung abgeleitet wurde. Zuletzt analysierten die Studierenden einen neuen Fall ohne Peer-Feedback. Mittels einer hierarchischen Clusteranalyse wurden drei Cluster unterschiedlicher Integrationsmuster identifiziert: „Gegenseitige Bestätigung“, „Konfliktidentifikation“ und „Punktuelle Auswahl“. Die Prädiktoren und Outcomes unterschieden sich insbesondere bei dem Integrationsmuster „Punktuelle Auswahl“: Studierende, die dieses Integrationsmuster zeigten, hatten akkurateres, jedoch weniger relevantes und umsetzbares Feedback erhalten. Entsprechend wurde dieses Feedback auch weniger häufig umgesetzt. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass unterschiedliche objektive Feedbackeigenschaften zu unterschiedlichen Mustern bei der Integration von multiplen Peer-Feedback-Nachrichten führen und dass diese Muster den Umfang der Nutzung dieses Peer-Feedbacks beeinflussen. Die Effektivität der Integration multipler Peer-Feedback-Nachrichten könnte künftig durch adaptive Interventionen unterstützt werden.

Show details
Authors:

Prof. Dr. Carla Bohndick | Universität Hamburg

Im Hochschulkontext gelten Sprach- und Lesekompetenz als zentrale Voraussetzung für Studienwahl und einen erfolgreichen Studienverlauf (Talwar et al., 2023). Frühere Forschung zeigt, dass sprachliches Selbstkonzept, realistische Bildungserwartungen und vorherige Leistungen Bildungsentscheidungen junger Menschen prägen (Horlboge et al., 2025; Möller & Trautwein, 2020). Obwohl die Bedeutung von Sprachkompetenz im Bildungskontext unbestritten ist, bleibt Forschung im Bereich der Hochschulbildung bislang unterrepräsentiert.
Die vorliegende Studie auf Basis des Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies (PIAAC) analysiert daher die Lesekompetenz deutscher Hochschulstudierender (Zyklus 1: n = 316; Zyklus 2: n = 352), um sprachbezogene Herausforderungen beim Übergang ins Studium und während dessen Verlauf zu identifizieren. Der Fokus liegt dabei auf (1) Unterschieden zwischen Studierenden, Nicht-Studierenden und unterschiedlichen Subgruppen sowie der Frage, (2) ob hohe Lesekompetenzen die Studienfachwahl beeinflussen.
Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass Studierende insgesamt eine deutlich höhere Lesekompetenz zeigen als nicht-studierende Erwachsene (Δ= 44.49; p < .001). Gleichzeitig sind nur zwischen 1 und 4 Prozent der Studierenden im deutschen gering literalisiert. Zudem zeigt sich, dass Studierende der ersten Generation nur geringfügig schlechter abschneiden als Studierende aus akademischen Elternhäusern (Δ=10.62; p = .023). Die Befunde implizieren, dass Studierende trotz unterschiedlicher sozialer Herkunft mit ähnlichen sprachlichen Herausforderungen konfrontiert werden.
Zudem wird diskutiert, ob stärkere Lesekompetenzen die Wahl sprachintensiver Studiengänge begünstigt und ob Frauen aufgrund ihres im Durchschnitt höheren sprachlichen Selbstkonzepts ebenfalls eher zu sprachlich komplexeren Studiengängen tendieren.
Insgesamt liefert die Studie neue Hinweise zur Bedeutung sprachlicher Kompetenzen im Hochschulbereich und zeigt, wie Lesefähigkeiten Studienerfolg und Studienwahlprozess beeinflussen können.

Dr. Jessica Gnas | Insitut für Bildungsanalysen Baden-Württemberg | Germany

Theoretical background: Data-based school development has become a central strategy in educational governance and school development. At the same time, research highlights that the mere availability of data does not automatically lead to in-formed decision-making; rather, meaningful data use depends on adequate data literacy and supportive tools such as dashboards.

Contribution: The “Schuldatenblatt” (translated as School Data Sheet) is a dashboard for data-based quality development in schools in Baden-Württemberg (Germany). It provides each school leader and its associated school supervision authority a compact overview of quality-relevant indicators (i.e., contextual conditions, processes, and outcomes of school quality). The paper conceptualizes the Schuldatenblatt as a supportive instrument that simultaneously operationalizes normative conceptions of school quality and structures professional data use.
The paper’s contribution furthermore lies in theorizing the Schuldatenblatt at the intersection of three research fields: (1) dashboard research, focusing on visualization, reduction of complexity, and decision support (e.g., Curran et al., 2024); (2) data literacy research, addressing the competencies required to interpret and critically reflect on quality indicators (e.g., Lee et al., 2024); and (3) research on data-based school and instructional improvement, emphasizing the role of Big-Data in the context of an iterative data-use process (e.g., Schildkamp, 2019).

Implications: Drawing on the Schuldatenblatt, the paper discusses how dashboards can be designed and embedded to promote data literacy among school leaders and thereby enhance data-based quality development in schools.

Malin Müller | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Malin Müller | Germany
Dominique Maciejewski
Leonie Schorrlepp
Tanja Lischetzke
Leonie V.D.E. Vogelsmeier

Background: Detecting inattentive responding in experience sampling methods (ESM) is essential for ensuring data quality. Therefore, an increasing number of studies are developing quantitative methods to detect inattentive responding in ESM at the occasion level. However, recent findings show low alignment between these approaches, raising fundamental questions about what these approaches really capture. Evaluating such methods is constrained by the lack of ground truth in real-world data. Simulation-based validation therefore requires assumptions about the form of inattentive responding, which remain uncertain due to the same lack of ground truth. This methodological catch-22 leaves disagreements among methods unresolved.
Methods: To better understand what the quantitative methods capture, the present project adopts a mixed-methods approach by incorporating qualitative data on participants’ self-reported response processes at the measurement occasion level. The collected dataset comprises more than 4,000 measurement occasions where participants verbally elaborated on their numerical responses. Specifically, two quantitative models—a multilevel latent class analysis (ML-LCA) based on response time, invariability, and consistency indices, and a dynamic mixture item response theory model—are applied to the ESM data and triangulated with coded qualitative response processes to provide additional insight into the meaning of (non-)flagged occasions.
Results: For each quantitative method, we descriptively examine the distribution of response processes across (non-)flagged occasions, the length of qualitative descriptions (word counts), and the frequency of response-processes.
Conclusions: This triangulation is expected to clarify the substantive meaning of latent inattentive responding states derived from two quantitative models in ESM and to illuminate what (non-)flagged occasions represent.

288. Reducing Bias Against LGBTI+ People: Integrating Practitioners’ Perspectives and International Research Evidence
Dr. Ulrich Klocke | Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Dr. Ulrich Klocke | Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin | Germany
Dr. Sabine Lehmann-Grube | Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin | Germany

Many organizations implement interventions to counter bias against LGBTI+ people and promote an inclusive climate. We combined an analysis of interventions conducted in Germany with findings from international research on intervention effectiveness.
Two online surveys targeted organizations that implemented or coordinated interventions across Germany. In the first survey, 274 organizations reported 1,064 interventions, most involving direct contact with target groups such as educational professionals, managers, or students. Additional approaches included publicly valuing diversity, modifying organizational structures, and developing educational materials. Qualitative interviews with 30 implementers explored their goals and experiences with key conditions (moderators) for achieving them. Frequently cited moderators included fostering open discussion, valuing participants’ viewpoints, and encouraging reflection on privilege and discrimination. In the second survey, most frequently mentioned goals and moderators were assessed quantitatively.
To complement these insights, we conducted systematic searches in nine international databases spanning psychology, social sciences, economics, education, and medicine. Our review identified more than 1,000 studies—predominantly from the USA—examining interventions to reduce LGBTI+-related bias. Most focused on lesbian, gay, or transgender people, while bias against bisexual, asexual, or intersex people remained understudied. The studies largely addressed educational settings, intergroup contact (direct or indirect), and structural interventions such as support groups or policies. Although many used cross-sectional or simple pre–post designs, we concentrated on controlled experiments and longitudinal studies to allow stronger causal inferences.
Comparing practitioners’ approaches and expectations with empirical evidence, we outline promising directions for advancing both research and practice on reducing bias against LGBTI+ people.

Bereits existierende Instrumente beschränken sich auf Selbstwirksamkeitserleben, Einstellungen (z.B. Vantieghem et al., 2023), Wissen im Bereich Diagnostik und Intervention (König et al., 2017) sowie die qualitative Erfassung von Unterrichtsstrategien (Przibilla et al., 2016).
Ausgehend von diesem Forschungsstand wurde entsprechend der Kompetenzdefinition von Weinert (2001) ein Test entwickelt, mit dem neben der Erfassung von selbstberichteten Kompetenzen auch handlungsbezogene Kompetenzen gemessen werden sollen. Hierzu wurden anhand der Sichtung (inter-)nationaler inklusionsbezogener Veröffentlichungen und eines Expertinnengesprächs zunächst fünf Kompetenzbereiche identifiziert: Diagnostische Kompetenz, Entwicklung inklusiver Lernräume und -gelegenheiten, Förderung des Schüler*innenaustauschs, Zusammenarbeit mit Erziehungsberechtigten und Kolleg*innen und Umgang mit inklusionsbezogenem Stress. Anhand dieser Kompetenzbereiche wurden sowohl Selbsteinschätzungs- als auch Situationsbeurteilungsitems entwickelt. Die Items wurden im Zuge einer Delphi-Konsens-Studie (N = 5) weiterentwickelt und durch Studierende des Masters of Education (N = 93) bearbeitet. Anhand dieser Stichprobe wurde eine Itemselektion durchgeführt und die angenommene Faktorenstruktur mittels einer konfirmatorischen Faktorenanalyse unterstützt.
Zur weiteren Validierung wurde das Testinstrument in Kombination mit den inhaltsnahen und -fernen Instrumenten DISCO (Vantieghem et al., 2020) und BilWiss-2.0 (Kunina-Habenicht et al., 2020) durch Lehramtsstudierende (N ≈ 400) und Lehrkräfte (N ≈ 150) bearbeitet. Erste Ergebnisse dieser Stichprobe zeigen eine erneute Unterstützung der angenommenen Faktorenstruktur. Signifikante Korrelationen mit den externen Instrumenten unterstützen weiterhin die Konstruktvalidität unseres Instruments. Weitere Ergebnisse zur Validierung werden bis Sommer 2026 vorliegen.

Following efforts to improve the measurement of workaholism, recent international research focused on developing and validating multidimensional instruments. The present study describes the validation of a German version of the Multidimensional Workaholism Scale, consisting of items assessing the motivational, cognitive, emotional, and behavioral aspects of workaholism. A professional translation agency translated the original English version into German. To validate the new language version, 298 participants completed the German workaholism scale and several other questionnaires. Overall, the German Multidimensional Workaholism Scale showed good reliability and validity. The construct validity could be confirmed, as the workaholism scores were more strongly related to similar constructs, such as work addiction, than to different constructs, such as burnout. Furthermore, the originally postulated four-factor structure was largely supported in comparative confirmatory factor analyses. However, a bifactor model containing an additional general independent workaholism factor fit the data even better than a simple four-factor structure. Notably, measurement invariance tests conducted across groups differing in their age, job experience, employment type, sex, and education indicated that the instrument can be applied to some of these groups for group comparisons. Overall, the present results indicate that the German version of the Multidimensional Workaholism Scale is suitable for use in research to elucidate the role of workaholism in career development and health-related implications in the work context.

With the increasing flexibility of the workplace as consequence of the COVID-19-pandemic, the impact of working from home (WFH) on employee behavior has become increasingly relevant. While managing directors have called for the reduction of the home office, previous studies indicated positive and negative effects of remote work (Anakpo et al., 2023; Gajendran et al., 2024). However, effects of differences in work environment (facility, technology; Tleuken et al., 2022) and its interactions with personality have rarely been investigated with WFH. This study investigates how both Big Five personality traits and work environment influence (counter)productive work behavior, compared to office-based work.
Method: A sample of N = 106 employees (53 % females) with home office experience participated in a online survey comprised of items on personality traits (Rammstedt & John, 2005), home work environment (Tleuken et al., 2022), productivity (ibid.), counterproductive work behavior (CWB; Junça Silva & Martins, 2023) and cyberslacking (O’Neill et al., 2014) based on validated self-report measures. Data was analyzed by means of correlation/regression analysis.
Results and conclusion: Results showed that conscientiousness, home office work environment and a higher WFH proportion were positively related to productivity and negatively correlated with cyberslacking and CWB. Furthermore, conscientiousness moderates the relationship between the work environment and cyberslacking as well as CWB. The lower the conscientiousness of the employees, the stronger the correlation between working conditions and negative work behavior. These results highlight the importance of this combination of personality and work environment for work behavior in the home office.

292. Validation of an Objective Personality Test for measuring conscientiousness in a study selection process
Marcel Berger | Salzburg University | Germany
Show details
Author:
Marcel Berger | Salzburg University | Germany

Despite Cattell’s longstanding conceptualization of behavior-based personality tests and new possibilities due to technological advances, there is still a lack of standardized instruments and empirical findings. Given the robust link between conscientiousness and academic as well as job performance, professional aptitude assessments would benefit from personality measures that are less susceptible to response distortion. The present study therefore aimed to evaluate the psychometric properties of the newly developed Objective Self Control Test, designed to measure impulse control as a subdimension of conscientiousness. Data from 774 applicants collected during a study aptitude procedure was analyzed. In the test, participants were asked to identify the number of target objects in different presentation modalities. We assessed were correct/incorrect responses, response time and inaccuracy. Measures of attention as well as questionnaire-based personality scores served as external validation criteria. Results revealed that longer response times were generally associated with fewer incorrect responses. The relation between correct responses and attention was weak. No significant association was revealed between questionnaire-based personality scores and the number of correct/incorrect items or inaccuracy. Psychometric challenges were low internal consistencies, partly ambiguous inter-item correlations, and in some cases high item difficulty. Overall, the Objective Self Control Test lays foundation for assessing conscientiousness through a short performance task. Particular attention must be given to defining adequate cut-off values for treating outliers in response time patterns and counting inaccuracy. Future research may revise item material in terms of presentation modalities and conduct an further validation study to address criterion validity in different fields.

Social, emotional, and behavioral (SEB) skills represent individuals' capacities to manage relationships, regulate emotions, and pursue goals. While personality traits have been extensively studied across the lifespan, less is known about the developmental patterns of SEB skills. This study examines whether SEB skills demonstrate similar stability and changeability as personality traits in young adults. Approximately 400 U.S. young adults completed assessments of the Behavioral, Emotional, and Social Skills Inventory (BESSI; 96 items) and HEXACO personality traits (100 items) at baseline, 6-month, and 12-month intervals. We compare rank-order stability, mean-level change, and individual-level change between SEB skills and personality traits. Due to ongoing data collection, study results are not yet available at time of submission. Given that SEB skills are explicitly conceptualized as learnable capabilities, we expect comparable or greater change in SEB skills relative to personality traits. 294. A Comparison of Finite Mixture and Score-Based Partitioning Approaches to Detecting Response Process Heterogeneity with Item Response Tree Models
Dr. Emre Alagöz | Universität Mannheim | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Dr. Emre Alagöz | Universität Mannheim | Germany
Prof Thorsten Meiser | Universität Mannheim | Germany
Dr Rudolf Debelak | University of Zurich | Switzerland

Response styles (RS), tendencies to choose specific response options regardless of item content, pose a threat to the validity of self-report data. To account for the effects of RS, researchers can use IRTree models. IRTrees decompose ordinal responses into pseudo-items that represent decision-making processes, so that various factors driving category choices to be modeled. However, traditional IRTrees assume that all respondents use the same processes during responding. Earlier research with mixture and score-based partitioning (SBP) approaches found that different groups of respondents can follow different response strategies, proving that the traditional "one-size-fits-all" assumption may not be suitable for accounting for RS effects.
The mixture and SBP approaches to IRTree models have major differences in how they capture response process heterogeneity. Mixture models use the response vectors of individuals to find latent classes of respondents who follow distinct measurement models. Optionally, one can explore the effects of covariates (e.g., demographics) on class memberships. The SBP approach, in contrast, makes use of external variables to search for individual misfit and recursively splits the sample to discover subgroups that follow different measurement models, minimizing the misfit.
To better understand the conceptual differences between mixture and SBP methods and to provide evidence-based guidance to users, we conducted a series of simulation studies. We found that neither method is universally superior; rather, factors like the reliability of covariates, their effect on group membership, sample size, and test length determine the performance of the two methods regarding various outcomes, such as model selection and classification accuracy.

295. SMART-, WOOP- oder doch lieber Motto-Ziele? Mediierende Einflüsse von Vitalität und Selbstwirksamkeit auf Unterschiede im Zielfortschritt in Abhängigkeit von Zielformulierung und autonomer vs. kontrollierter Zielmotivation
Tamara Hecht | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Tamara Hecht | Germany
Dr. Cathleen Kappes

Bisherige Studien vergleichen selten den Effekt verschiedener Zielformulierungsinterventionen und ihre Mediatoren direkt miteinander und berücksichtigen dabei nicht die Ausprägung der Zielmotivation (Self Determination Theory). Unsere Studie mit Lehramtsstudierenden (N = 301, 76% weiblich) untersucht den Unterschied im Zielfortschritt zwischen Motto-, SMART- und WOOP-Zielformulierungen im Vergleich zu einer Kontrollgruppe (between-subjects) bei autonomer und kontrollierter Zielmotivation (within-subjects; experimentell induziert) und damit verbundene Mediatoren wie Vitalität, Affekt und Selbstwirksamkeit.
Eine Pfadanalyse zeigt, dass autonom motivierte Ziele sowohl direkt als auch mediiert über Vitalität, positiven Affekt und Selbstwirksamkeit zu einem höheren Zielfortschritt führen als kontrolliert motivierte Ziele. Darüber hinaus wurde aufgedeckt, dass die SMART-Gruppe im Vergleich zur Kontrollgruppe bei autonomen Zielen einen höheren Zielfortschritt aufweist, während die Motto-Gruppe einen indirekten Effekt auf den Zielfortschritt hat. Bei kontrollierten Zielen wirkt die Motto-Gruppe über den Mediator Vitalität auf den Zielfortschritt, wohingegen der direkte Effekt negativ ausfällt und der totale Effekt keine Signifikanz erreicht.
Die Ergebnisse stützen die Annahme, dass die SMART-Zielsetzung den Zielfortschritt erhöht, wenn das Ziel auf persönlichen Werten und Interessen basiert. Bei als Verpflichtung wahrgenommen Zielen scheinen SMART-Ziele den Zielfortschritt hingegen nicht unterstützen zu können. Außerdem weisen die Ergebnisse darauf hin, dass verschiedene Wirkmechanismen von Motto-Zielen sich gegenseitig aufheben und in einem Nulleffekt resultieren. Die Motto-Zielsetzung scheint als Verpflichtung empfundene Ziele durch eine Steigerung der erlebten Vitalität stärken zu können, während sie bei autonomen Zielen durch die Mediatoren, insbesondere Selbstwirksamkeit, indirekt negativ wirkt. Offen bleibt, ob und welche Wirkmechanismen die WOOP-Zielsetzung verglichen zur Kontrollgruppe aufweist, da in dieser Studie keine Effekte festgestellt werden konnten.

296. „My Mii’s Hopes and Fears“ – Übernehmen Spielende motivspezifische Eigenschaften ihrer Avatare?

Show details
Authors:
Dr. Marianne Schneider | Universität Osnabrück | Germany
Sarah Eglin | Universisität Osnabrück
Jonas Schemann | Universität Osnabrück

Aus der Avatarforschung ist bekannt, dass Spielende von Videospielen Merkmale übernehmen können, die sie ihren Avataren stereotyp zuschreiben. Dieser sogenannte Proteus-Effekt wurde häufig mittels äußerlicher Merkmale wie Größe oder Attraktivität untersucht. Darauf aufbauend stellt sich die Frage, ob eine solche Übernahme auch bei Eigenschaften wie z.B. Erfolgszuversicht oder Misserfolgsängstlichkeit erfolgen kann. Um dies herauszufinden, wurden in einem einfaktoriellen Between-Subjects-Experiment 60 Personen von 19 bis 39 Jahren (M = 23.8 Jahre, 77% weiblich, 93% Studierende) untersucht. Diesen wurde entweder ein Avatar zugewiesen, der sich ihnen in einem Video als erfolgszuversichtlich präsentierte, oder einer, der misserfolgsängstlich war. Mit diesem digitalen Stellvertreter ihrer selbst spielten sie nach einer kurzen Probephase fünf Runden eines Balancierspiels auf einer Wii-Konsole. Vor jeder Runde sollten sie sich ein Ziel setzen, nach jeder Runde wurden sie nach den Ursachen für das Erreichen oder Nichterreichen des Ziels gefragt sowie nach ihren diesbezüglichen Gefühlen. Basierende auf dem Selbstbewertungsmodell von Heckhausen wurde angenommen, dass Personen mit einem erfolgszuversichtlichen Avatar a) sich realistischere Ziele setzen, b) Erfolge stärker auf internale und weniger auf externale Faktoren zurückführen, c) Misserfolge stärker auf variable und weniger auf internal stabile Faktoren zurückführen, d) bei Erfolgen mehr positive Gefühle, insbesondere Stolz, erwähnen und e) bei Misserfolgen von weniger negativen Gefühlen, insbesondere Scham, berichten als Personen mit einem misserfolgsängstlichen Avatar. Entgegen den Erwartungen zeigten sich keine Gruppenunterschiede bezüglich der Zielsetzung sowie der Attribution von Misserfolgen auf variable Faktoren. Alle anderen Annahmen ließen sich jedoch bestätigen. Diese Ergebnisse werden u.a. hinsichtlich der Nutzung von Avataren in Lernsettings diskutiert.

297. Rethinking the Measurement of Interrogative Suggestibility: A Working Model
Jonas Bellinghausen | Bonn Universität | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Jonas Bellinghausen | Bonn Universität | Germany
Alexandra Jaworek
Dr. Merlin Monzel

Interrogative suggestibility is of significant relevance in contemporary research and applied settings.
In practice, the Gudjonsson Suggestibility Scale (GSS) has become widely accepted as the standard for measuring this trait. It is a text-based procedure that uses covert deception. This requirement makes “uninformed subjects” indispensable and complicates the interpretation of individual test results if subjects recognize the deception during the procedure.

Therefore, we developed the Visual Imagery Suggestibility Task (VIST), an image-based test that does not rely on covert deception and can be administered repeatedly.
At the outset, the test subjects are informed about the use of deception in certain stimuli. However, it is not apparent to subjects which items contain deceptive elements. This makes the test suitable for testing “informed subjects” for example measuring changes.

The VIST was validated using the established GSS with a sample of 230 subjects. The results show a moderate correlation between the two scales. The reason for the moderate correlations will be critically discussed. On the one hand, the VIST differs from the GSS in terms of procedure and stimulus material. Nevertheless, it would be useful to revise and further develop both the stimulus material and the procedure of the VIST based on the available results.

Overall, the results indicate a fundamentally equivalent test procedure which, after a few adjustments, could be put into practice. Furthermore, the VIST could serve as a blueprint for making suggestibility measurable with other sensory modalities.

298. Beyond Accuracy and Self-Enhancement: How Body Appreciation Buffers Self-Esteem from Mate Value Discrepancies

People routinely overestimate their attractiveness, yet this self-enhancement can be either adaptive (supporting self-worth) or maladaptive (distorting reality). Body appreciation–acceptance of one's body independent of appearance standards–may determine when discrepancies in mate value threaten versus spare self-esteem. We examined: (1) How do self-assessed and externally rated mate value relate to body appreciation? (2) Does body appreciation moderate the association between mate value discrepancy and self-esteem?
Ninety-six adults (60% female, M_age = 28.1) completed self-assessments of mate value, body appreciation, and self-esteem. Eight independent raters evaluated mate value from photographs. We examined congruence and incongruence effects between self- and other-rated mate value on body appreciation using response surface analysis. Moderation analysis tested whether body appreciation buffered effects of mate value discrepancy on self-esteem.
Body appreciation correlated with self-assessed and externally rated mate value. Response surface analysis revealed body appreciation increased when self and external ratings aligned, with overestimation trending toward higher body appreciation than underestimation. A significant moderation effect emerged: Among individuals low in body appreciation, self-esteem was positively associated with overestimation, whereas no significant association emerged for those high in body appreciation.
Body appreciation enabled self-esteem maintenance regardless of agreement between self and external attractiveness ratings, providing a resilience pathway distinct from accurate self-assessment or self-enhancement.

Authors:

Interference between cognitive control and control of body balance is well documented but remains poorly understood. We developed an event-related approach to examine these cross-domain interactions on a subsecond timescale. Using cognitive conflict tasks, such as a Simon, Spatial Stroop or Flanker tasks, we observed reduced force moment variability (indicator of balance control) during response selection in the cognitive conflict task. We interpret this reduction as transient inhibition or delay of balance adjustments caused by competition for shared processing resources (“micro-bottleneck”). Previous studies showed that this interference occurred mainly along the mediolateral (ML) body axis, matching the decision-making frame of the cognitive conflict tasks. The present study investigated whether this axis-specific effect could be altered by changing the direction of decision making. Two experiments using 2D Spatial Stroop tasks were conducted: one requiring response along the mediolateral (ML) axis and the other along the anteroposterior (AP) axis. Experiment order was counterbalanced across 90 young adult participants. Unexpectedly, the ML task produced reduced variability along the AP axis, while no transient reduction was observed in the AP task. The AP shift in the ML task may reflect target-directed attentional or oculomotor processes misaligned with decision direction. The absence of interference in the AP task may result from longer processing times and weaker congruency effects. Nevertheless, both tasks showed systematic modulation of force moment variability across trials, with gradual reductions after target onset and minima during response selection. This pattern suggests dynamic adaptation of balance control to periods of increased cognitive demand.

Extracting route information from maps is essential for many wayfinding tasks and is influenced by both cognitive abilities and map-reading skills. Map-reading skills develop through everyday experience with maps. Because older adults relied on maps before navigation assistance systems became widespread, they are expected to have stronger map-reading skills than younger adults who grew up with assisted navigation. However, age-related cognitive decline may disadvantage older adults in map-based route learning. In other words, to succeed in this task, older adults may benefit from practiced map-reading skills, whereas younger adults benefit from higher spatial abilities. Therefore, this study examined age-related differences in the map-based route learning performance of younger (Mage = 21.32) and older adults (Mage = 65.51) and investigated the mediating role of visuospatial working memory (VSWM) capacity and perspective-taking ability (PTA) in the differences in navigation performance. 86 participants (41 old, 45 young) learned a route depicted on a digital map while their gaze patterns were recorded, and navigated the route from memory in a virtual environment. Navigation errors were recorded as a measure of route memory performance. Compared to older adults, younger adults demonstrated higher VSWM capacity and better PTA. Besides, they performed better in the navigation task, suggesting that cognitive abilities play a stronger role compared to map-reading skills. The association between age group and navigation errors was fully mediated by PTA, but not by WMC. Gaze patterns are currently being analyzed to gain insight into how they relate to performance.

People can be motivated to engage in collective action for climate protection because they are angry about an injustice or because they are emotionally moved by the idea that they can achieve something together. To date, specific elicitors of these emotions in the context of non-normative climate protests are unclear. One possible elicitor of these feelings is the anticipated success of the protest. However, it is not clear which criteria climate activists use to evaluate their actions. To better understand the motivation to engage in collective action for climate protection and the respective success criteria, we conducted structured interviews (N = 30) in Germany with activists of the “Last Generation”, a group that engages in non-normative collective action for climate protection. Qualitative content analyses revealed that feelings of being moved were mainly evoked by solidarity among activists, especially in threatening situations. Perceived success criteria mainly focused on raising awareness for the severity of climate change. The identified emotion elicitors as well as the success criteria enhance our understanding of sustained collective climate action.

Prof. Dr. Elmar Souvignier | Universität Münster

Das geringe Niveau und die hohe Heterogenität von Leseleistungen in deutschen Grundschulen machen passgenaue, individuelle Förderung nötig. Ein Ansatz, individuelle Förderentscheidungen diagnosebasiert abzuleiten, ist Lernverlaufsdiagnostik. Lernverlaufsdiagnostik ist gekennzeichnet durch kurze, einfach durchführbare Tests mit guten psychometrischen Eigenschaften. Adaptives Testen ist eine ideale Möglichkeit zur Umsetzung, da es Messeffizienz maximiert und hohe Heterogenität in Schüler:innenleistungen berücksichtigen kann. Projektziel ist, einen für Lernverlaufsdiagnostik geeigneten, adaptiven Leseverständnistest für Dritt- und Viertklässler zu konzipieren. Dazu wird ein umfangreicher Itempool mit kurzen Aufgaben benötigt, der zuverlässig ein eindimensionales Konstrukt misst, ein breites Schwierigkeitsspektrum abdeckt und eine hohe konvergente Validität mit etablierten Verfahren aufweist.
Unter systematischer Variation schwierigkeitsgenerierender Merkmale (z.B. Präpositionen) wurden über 300 kurze Lesetexte (50-150 Wörter) mit 1-2 zugehörigen Verständnisfragen erstellt. Anschließend wurden die Items auf 25 Itemblöcke verteilt und in einem balancierten, unvollständigen Multiple-Matrix-Design in 25 Heften mit je 4 Itemblöcken an 650 Kindern im Schuljahr 2024/25 pilotiert.
Erste Ergebnisse der IRT-Analysen sprechen für die Annahme eines 1PL-Modells (1 PL vs. 2 PL; χ2(252) = 824,77, p < .001, 2-PL vs. 3-PL; χ2(253) = 326,89, p = .001). Der Aufgabenpool deckt dabei eine breite Schwierigkeitsspanne von -2,99 < θ < 2,35 ab. Zudem werden vertiefende Analysen in Hinblick auf Zuverlässigkeit und Zusammenhänge mit ELFE II, SLS, Wortschatz und Lesemotivation vorgestellt.
Die bislang vorliegenden Ergebnisse legen ein eindimensionales Konstrukt sowie eine für adaptive Tests erforderliche Schwierigkeitsstreuung nahe. Perspektivisch sollen die Items in eine Online-Lernverlaufsdiagnostik implementiert und in der Schulpraxis als adaptiver Lesetest evaluiert werden.

303. Context and feedback shape the balance of learning and decision dynamics: A reinforcement learning-diffusion decision modelling approach
Nicola Schneider | Heidelberg University | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Nicola Schneider | Heidelberg University | Germany
Andreas Voss | Heidelberg University | Germany

Human decision-making in uncertain environments depends not only on how individuals learn from experience but also on how contextual factors modulate this learning. The present project investigates how environmental valence (win vs. loss domain) and feedback availability (full vs. partial) jointly shape value learning and evidence accumulation. N = 180 participants completed an adapted two-stage decision-making task in which transitions between states follow a Markovian structure, while the above manipulations induce systematic shifts in motivational and informational context. We compared model-free and model-based learning algorithms embedded within a reinforcement learning-diffusion decision model framework that maps subjective value differences onto drift rate and overall value context onto decision thresholds. This approach allowed us to quantify how learning strategies translate into temporal decision dynamics. We further tested the condition effects of environmental valence and feedback availability on cognitive parameters. Hierarchical Bayesian model comparison results reveal the best fit for model-free learning algorithms. Both environmental valence and feedback availability interact with learning rates, with higher learning rates in the win domain and the partial feedback condition. Feedback availability influences non-decision time and accuracy. The study offers a way to characterize how motivational and informational factors modulate the interplay between model-free and model-based learning and the dynamics of evidence accumulation. We discuss how the findings advance a mechanistic understanding of adaptive decision-making.

304. Do Psychological Studies Meet Data Protection Requirements? Evidence from Consent Form Analyses and Data Access Requests
Luisa Jansen | University of Bern | Switzerland
Show details
Authors:
Luisa Jansen | University of Bern | Switzerland
Annika Külpmann
Josephine Schär
Malte Elson | University of Bern

Psychological researchers have an ethical obligation to protect the data entrusted to them by their participants. Within the European Union, this obligation is further reinforced by the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), The GDPR governs, among other aspects, participants’ rights to information at the time of data collection, the procedures for obtaining consent to data processing, and the rights to access or request deletion of personal data after study participation. Compliance with these requirements is essential for maintaining participants’ trust in researchers and the research process.
Despite their importance, no empirical investigations have systematically examined whether psychological research projects comply with these obligations.
We present results from two preregistered studies on these issues. First, we conducted a content analysis of 101 consent forms used in psychological studies between 2019 and 2021, assessing their compliance with GDPR requirements and their correspondence with the data types reported in the associated publications. Results indicate that every consent form showed at least some degree of non-compliance with the researchers’ legal obligations under the GDPR. This suggests that researchers rely more on ethical norms than on these concrete legal requirements. Second, a research assistant participated in 100 psychological studies, after which she requested access to her personal data processed by the researchers, again observing their compliance with the GDPR. We will present the results of both studies and discuss their implications for research practice in psychological science.

305. Entwicklungssteuerung als Potential -Verstehen sich junge Erwachsene als ‚Ko-Produzent*innen‘ eigener Entwicklung ?-
Ass.-Prof. Dr. Jan Philipp Amadeus Aden | Sigmund Freud Privatuniversität Wien | Austria
Show details
Authors:
Ass.-Prof. Dr. Jan Philipp Amadeus Aden | Sigmund Freud Privatuniversität Wien | Austria
Eva Dreher

Hintergrund:

Eine zentrale Herausforderung der Entwicklungsetappe des frühen Erwachsenenalters ist die Übernahme von Verantwortung bei der Wahl von Zielen und Handlungsentscheidungen. Der Gewinn an Autonomie korrespondiert mit dem Erkennen der Bedeutung internaler und externaler Entwicklungsbedingungen und der Bewusstheit, den eigenen Entwicklungsprozess (situativ und prospektiv) durch aktive Steuerung von Einflussgrößen regulieren zu können.
Der vorliegenden Studie sind zwei Fragen zentral: (1) In welchem Maße nehmen junge Erwachsene ausgewählte Entwicklungsbedingungen als steuernd wahr; (2) Worin sehen sie Möglichkeiten, Entwicklungsbedingungen durch eigenes Handeln zu modifizieren?

Methode:

Die Untersuchung basiert auf einer Befragung von n=105 Studierenden im Alter von 18-29 Jahren. Zur Erfassung der Einschätzung der Steuerung individueller Entwicklung durch unterschiedliche Entwicklungsbedingungen wurde ein Instrument entwickelt und faktorenanalytisch sowie reliabilitätsanalytisch untersucht. Jeder identifizierte Faktor repräsentiert eine Entwicklungsbedingung mit jeweils zugeschriebener Einflussstärke.
Pro Entwicklungsbedingung wurde ein Ankeritem definiert, zu dem subjektive Handlungsmöglichkeiten zur Einflussreduktion offen erfasst und inhaltsanalytisch ausgewertet wurden.

Ergebnisse:

Vier identifizierte Faktoren erklären 59.21% der Gesamtvarianz und weisen durchgehend zufriedenstellende Reliabilitäten auf. Sie repräsentieren zugeschriebene Entwicklungseinflüsse durch Autonomes Geschehen, Aleatorisches Geschehen, Externale Bedingungen und Strukturelle Voraussetzungen (Ressourcenallokation). Externalen wird der stärkste, aleatorischen Bedingungen der schwächste Einfluss zugeschrieben.
Das Spektrum genannter Einflussmöglichkeiten umfasst selbstregulative, interpersonelle und lösungsorientierte Handlungsstrategien.

Konklusion:

Die handlungsorientierten Regulierungsvorschläge zeigen, dass internal autonome Aspekte wie biologische Komponenten nicht als entwicklungsdeterministisch, sondern als relevante Ausgangsbedingungen für Entwicklungseinflüsse verstanden werden. Externalen Bedingungen wird zwar der stärkste Einfluss zugeschrieben; gleichzeitig gelten sie aber durch individuelle Handlungsparameter als grundsätzlich regulierbar. Als nicht beeinflussbar gelten aleatorische Komponenten, deren Folgen aber durch regulatives Handeln bewältigt werden können.

306. Situationships als Ausdruck der Vagheit im Emerging Adulthood
Hannah Bruckner | Sigmund Freud PrivatUniversität (SFU) | Austria
Show details
Authors:
Hannah Bruckner | Sigmund Freud PrivatUniversität (SFU) | Austria
Iris Enengl | Sigmund Freud PrivatUniversität (SFU) | Austria

Hintergrund:

Situationships bezeichnen romantische Beziehungen ohne klare Definition oder Verbindlichkeit. Aufgrund von Ambiguität, inkonsistenten Erwartungen und fehlender Statusklärung können sie mit erhöhter psychischer Belastung einhergehen. Unklar ist bislang ihre Bedeutung im Entwicklungsprozess, insbesondere ob Situationships primär als Ausdrucksform des gesellschaftlichen Wandels von Beziehungen oder als Ausdruck entwicklungsphasenspezifischer Vagheit im Spannungsfeld zwischen Autonomie und Bindung zu verstehen sind.
Ziel ist es, Situationships aus Betroffenensicht zu explorieren und subjektiv positive sowie belastende Aspekte zu erfassen und deren Zusammenhang mit zentralen Charakteristika des Emerging Adulthood zu untersuchen.

Methode:

Befragt werden 18–29-Jährige in einem aktuell unverbindlichen romantischen Kontext mittels Online-Erhebung.
Dabei wird das Erleben von Situationships anhand von Charakteristika wie Angst, Vermeidung, Unsicherheit, sowie die dadurch erlebte Belastung erfasst. Außerdem werden Beziehungsansprüche entlang ausgewählter Dimensionen, sowie die aktuelle Zufriedenheit mit diesen erhoben.
Das Erleben entwicklungsphasenspezifischer Merkmale wird standardisiert mittels IDEA-G2 erfasst.
Die Auswertung umfasst deskriptive und korrelative Analysen sowie eine Clusteranalyse zur Identifikation unterschiedlicher Personentypen.

Ergebnisse:

Die Datenerhebung läuft aktuell, die Ergebnisse werden Anfang März erwartet. Erwartet wird, dass Situationships als belastend erlebt werden und Beziehungsansprüche und die aktuelle Zufriedenheit mit diesen Diskrepanzen aufweisen. Außerdem werden inhaltlich und empirisch trennscharfe Personentypen erwartet, die sich vor allem entlang der Art und des Ausmaßes an Belastung unterscheiden. Es wird erwartet, dass Situationships mit erhöhter erlebter Instabilität einhergehen.

Zusammenfassung:

Die Studie soll zu einem differenzierten Verständnis von Situationships im Emerging Adulthood beitragen und diese als soziales Phänomen mit potenziellen Entwicklungsrisiken und -chancen beleuchten. Basierend auf den resultierenden Personentypen sollen Implikationen für die beratende Praxis abgeleitet werden.

307. Do Meta-Emotions Mirror Primary Emotions? An Analysis of Emotional Response Profiles
Prof. Dr. Roland Neumann | Universität Trier | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Prof. Dr. Roland Neumann | Universität Trier | Germany
Dr. Vsevolod Scherrer | Universität Trier | Germany

The current research examines whether the quality of negative meta-emotions mirrors the quality of negative primary emotions. Such mirroring might hinge on an overlap in the processes underlying primary emotions and meta-emotions. Since such an overlap may be due to habitual tendencies to experience negative meta-emotions, Study 1 (N = 97) introduced a questionnaire assessing dispositional tendencies toward negative meta-emotions (Trait Meta-Emotion Questionnaire, TMEQ). Results showed that between-person differences were captured by the TMEQ. Moreover, TMEQ scores are associated with experimentally induced negative meta-emotions, rumination, emotion suppression, and life satisfaction. Finally, the quality of meta-emotions partially mirrored the quality of primary emotions. In Study 2 (N = 103), we manipulated reappraisal processes and found that both primary emotions and meta-emotions were influenced by appraisal processes. We replicated the finding that meta-emotions partially mirrored the quality of primary emotions. In addition, an acceptance manipulation that was intended to selectively influence meta-emotions did not significantly reduce the intensity of negative meta-emotions. In sum, our results support the assumption that the quality of meta-emotions partially mirrors the quality of primary emotions. Further, both primary emotions and meta-emotions were influenced by appraisal processes. The implications of our findings are discussed.
